reviews.name: Rui Miguel Da Silva Pinto
reviews.text: I am biased as I am timorese and love history, however the place is pretty run down, no signage and without people like me to suggest friends and colleagues visiting Timor to come and see it, few people would visit. I understand it may be hard to people living nearby to keep this place up and running on a volunteer basis, I would love to contribute and redo/re print the panels, However I do not know who is managing this, but what I came to know it that the place is closed on Saturday and Sunday, which I was not aware off nor did I see any signs, I opened the door the panels were there, went with some visitors in wanted to leave the usual contributions, did not see anybody, no signing book or collection box, 15 minutes after got a very angry Auntie, saying that the place was closed. I explained I did not know as there was no sign, the door was not locked, the only door locked was to door granting access to the restaurant. Despite me best efforts to say sorry in both tetun and Portuguese, I suppose auntie was having a very bad day...but still sad that we do not have a way of helping this place...

reviews.name: Vanda Day
reviews.text:
The Local Hangout: Dili’s Favorite Seaside Park

​If you're looking for the heart of Dili’s afternoon scene, this park is it. It’s where everyone heads for a sunset stroll or just to kick back and relax.

​Why People Love It: ​Fresh Coconuts: You’ll find plenty of vendors nearby selling fresh young coconuts. There’s nothing better than sipping on one right there while catching the breeze. ​The Digital Hub: One of the biggest draws is the free Wi-Fi. Don’t be surprised if you see groups of young people everywhere with their laptops out—it’s the unofficial outdoor office and study lounge of the city. ​Vibe & Cleanliness: Overall, the park is kept pretty tidy and has a great atmosphere.

​A Quick Heads-up: While there are public toilets available, the cleanliness is... well, a bit hit-or-miss. You might want to keep that in mind before you get too settled!

​Whether you’re there to browse the web or just people-watch with a drink in hand, it’s a great slice of local life.

title: Manny Timor Tours
ownerDescription:
Manny Timor Tours was established in 2019 by an experienced local tour operator to cater to the growing demand for travel and tourism services across Timor Island. From Jaco Island to Rote Island, our specialty is to facilitate visitors’ access to seldom-explored villages and communities and provide guests with full cultural immersion and genuine travel experiences. Our extensive experience in accessing traditional areas allows us to tailor activities and itineraries to the age and desires of our clientele.

We work with the local community to ensure their traditions and culture are preserved as the tourism industry grows in Timor. Our tours provide financial support for local people and the opportunity to share their unique ways of life

reviews.text: As an Australian based Travel Agent (Darwin) I have specialised in Timor-Leste for almost 8 years and throughout that time my go to tour operator has been Manny Timor Tours. reviews.name: Kirsten Enders
reviews.text: I have had the pleasure of taking seven trips in Timor with Manny Napoleon and his drivers over 11 years.  Five trips with students and two with friends. Manny is reliable knowledgeable organised friendly and his drivers are fantastic. We visit more remote areas where the roads are 4 WD only and the drivers handle the conditions with skill care and good humour. They are excellent company and end up being friends. I look forward to many more tours with Manny!

reviews.name: Marcus Fielding
reviews.text: Three of us revisited some old haunts from 1999. We travelled to Dili, Batugade, Balibo, Maliana, Bobonaro, Suai, Ainaro, Maubisse, Aileau and Baucau by 4WD. Our driver and Guide - Serafim - was terrific! He had great driving skills and was able to tell us a lot about the country, its history and its people. We changed our itinerary as we travelled, and the head office was able to make changes for us quickly and easily. We would highly recommend Manny Timor Tours.

reviews.name: Ben and Brenda Bruce
reviews.text: We had a fantastic trip. Alex was such a great guide. He was able to tweak the schedule to our needs and was great with our kids. He so generously shared his personal experiences of the Timor liberation, the feeling he described will stay with us for a long time. We will tell anyone who listens to come and visit Dili and use this service. It added a depth of meaning to our trip that I don’t think you could find in just wandering about. We are so grateful that we could learn from Alex and have him share his knowledge with us.
reviews.responseFromOwnerText: Thank you Brenda, Ben and the Boys. Appreciate your support 👏🤝🙏

reviews.name: Mark Davies
reviews.text:
An Unforgettable Day Trip to Balibó
Manny Tours Timor delivered an absolutely outstanding full-day experience to Balibó a place of profound historical significance as the site where the Balibo Five were tragically murdered. It’s a sobering and deeply moving destination, and having a knowledgeable guide made all the difference in understanding the weight of what happened there.
Fair warning to anyone booking this tour: the road to Balibó is rough, with extensive roadworks along the way, so be prepared for a bumpy ride. That said, it’s absolutely worth every pothole. The journey itself is part of the adventure, offering incredible scenery through the Timorese countryside.
A highlight we didn’t expect was a visit to the Indonesian border, which added a fascinating geopolitical dimension to the day and really put the history of the region into context.
A special mention must go to our guide Jonias, who was exceptional knowledgeable, passionate about the history of Timor-Leste, and a genuine pleasure to spend the day with. If you’re visiting Timor-Leste and want to go beyond Dili, this tour with Manny Tours is a must. Ask for Jonias you won’t be disappointed. 5 stars without hesitation

reviews.name: Robbert Bakker
reviews.text:
A few years ago I wrote a book about the trials and tribulations of the Dutch colonial army of the former Dutch East Indies (KNIL) and the Australian commandos against the Imperial Japanese Army during WWII on Timor. This was requested by daughters and sons of these Dutch (which includes many people with Indonesian roots) veterans. A friend of mine persuaded me to visit Timor and all these places. So we went this summer, for which I'm very grateful to him. But where to start? This certain part of history was all so very specific. Manny Timor Tours was the only company that made a specific itinerary about WWII (including the lesser known Dutch participation) on the entire island of Timor. And it was also their first time - my compliments.

We had Serafim as our guide, a very nice and accessible man that really made our trip. He knows six forms of Tetum and endlessly translated for us, which truly enhanced our experience of the history of Timor, having many conversations with elderly Timorese about WWII, the Portuguese colonisation and the Indonesian occupation and subsequent chaos and massacres. It was emotional, but Serafim really did well. He was also very flexible in his time schedule, so nothing is super 'fixed'. If you book with Manny Timor Tours, request Serafim. And finally, he is a good driver - and believe me - that is no unnecessary luxury on Timor! The island is beautiful, but some roads are quite hard to navigate and a good driver really makes the difference.

When you go of the beaten track, do not expect any Western luxuries, but you have to embrace this. Many Timor Tours tries its utmost best to make you as comfortable as possible. Be it a good car or a good accommodation. Timor-Leste is a new nation, not even 20 years have passed since the last big troubles. Be nice and respectful towards a nation that is building its nationhood and has known more massacres in the last 25 years than we can name. The Timorese are very friendly and if you love unspoiled nature, this is your spot. And if you're interested in the WWII history of Timor, Manny Timor Tours is the company for you. They took us all around the island, from Díli to Ataúro island, Viqueque, Tutuala and unspoiled Jaco island in the east, Atambua, Soe and Kupang in the west. No place is too far. Also, don't repeat my mistake by focusing to much on the Portuguese language, as it is rarely spoken anymore. Tetum and Indonesian are the languages to go on Timor! And the international language is English now, not Portuguese anymore.

Have fun and enjoy this extraordinary island.

reviews.name: Jelle de Vries
reviews.text:
We did a 14 day tour from Timor-Leste to West-Timor. Started in Dìli, Ataúro, Mount Ramelau, Suai, Samé, Loihuno, Tutuàla, Jaco Island, Baucau, Liquica, Balibó, Atambua, Soé, Kupang. In Timor-Leste our guide and driver Serafim really went out of his way to give us the best experience. He was also a great travelling companion, translated a lot of stories of local Timorese and told us a lot about the country by his own experience. We fell in love with the beautiful nature and had a great time with the people. What really stood out in the tour that we also saw the difficult history of Timor-Leste (colonial times, WO II and Indonesian time). This gave the full picture. Everything was arranged for us but they were very flexible with what we wanted to do- a mix between some beach/ snorkelling time and also some historical information/ museums and markets. They even got up early for us one morning to do a sunrise walk up Cristo Rei at our request.

The highlight of the trip was a day tour to Balibo with lunch at the forte and a walking tour of the local village. The roads there were a bit rough in places but felt very safe in a 4WD with Lito as our experienced local driver.

On an Atauro island day trip a local guide, Erni, came with us to help find snorkelling gear/ lunch/ transport on the island itself.

reviews.name: Yonatan Romero

I just finished an incredible tour to Maubessi that I can't recommend enough! The landscapes were breathtaking, and the activities were well-planned and enjoyable. One of the best parts was visiting traditional houses and interacting with the locals, who were all so friendly. I even got to try some homemade coffee, which was absolutely delicious!

The transportation was modern and comfortable, making the journey a pleasure. My guide, Serefim, was fantastic! He was not only friendly but also shared fascinating insights about the culture and history of the area. He made sure to stop at all the key highlights and captured some beautiful photos along the way.

As a solo traveler, I felt completely at ease and thoroughly enjoyed every moment of the tour. If you're considering this experience, go for it! You won't be disappointed!

reviews.name: Sylvain Cuperlier
reviews.text:
I spent ten days on a tour with Manny Timor Tours. It first started by contacting the agency  to customise the tour. Lito, and then Erin, were very responsive and helpful. In the end, we decided to take bits and pieces of existing packages and ended up with a tour starting from Dili, going the to Mount Ramelau, Suai in the Southern Coast, Same, Betano, Viqueque, Ossù, Mondo Perdido, Veniliale, Baucau, Los Palos, Tutuala, Jaco Island, Com and then back to Dili through Baucau. This tour was a good mix between hiking, including the ascent of Mount Ramelau to see the wonderful sunrise, beach activities, and history, from the Portuguese colony to the Japanese attacks during WWII and, more recently, the massacres related to the Indonesian occupation.

Alex, my guide was very friendly and knowledgeable, particularly of the history during the occupation times. In addition to fully following the programme, he also sometimes went for the extra-mile, for example when we visited one of his friends’ farm in Los Palos. Alex is also knowledgeable about coffee and knows all the coffee-shops of Timor-Leste, and it was great to stop at the best ones to enjoy a good coffee and take a break from the (often) bumpy roads. In addition, Alex was a very safe driver and our 4x4 vehicle was robust enough to cross rivers when bridges were damaged.

So this was a remarkable experience, off the beaten tracks, particularly between Suai and Tutuala, where we did not meet any tourist at all.

As a consequence, one should be aware that while such a tour has its price (mainly because the local currency is the US dollar), the local standards may not be those regularly met in more touristic countries, particularly in the most remote areas that this tour allowed me to visit. The accommodation were clean and decent, but sometimes with no hot water and not always with en-suite bathrooms. So, if you are looking forward to relaxing in a jacuzzi with a glass of champagne after a busy hiking day, Timor-Leste may not be your place. Also, do not expect to have lunch at a fixed time, simply because, in some areas, you can spend hours on the road without seeing a decent place to have some food. Please also note that the roads can be unpredictable because of landslides or broken bridges. We made it every time but this may not always be the case.

So, be prepared for the adventure! At least Timor-Leste is still one of those countries allowing for it, while being a very friendly and safe country. With Many Timor Tours, you will feel safe and in good hands for enjoying this adventure.

There wasn't much information about the building at the time. The view from above, with its long coastline, is impressive. title: Galeria Memória Viva (Children and The Future Foundation)
subTitle: Galeria Memória Viva
ownerDescription:
Galeria Memória Viva is a gallery owned by H.E. Dr. José Ramos-Horta. Inside, it houses a wide variety of items, each with its own story, showcasing the life and legacy of Dr. Ramos-Horta. The gallery is open to the public and also provides a quiet space and books for students to study. All services are completely free — there is no cost to visit the gallery, study on-site, or access the books.
For group visits, please make an appointment in advance by contacting GMV staff through WhatsApp, Facebook, or Email.
Thank you.
address: Rua Sergio Viera de Mello, Díli, Timor-Leste

Embora enfrente desafios como o avanço de materiais sintéticos e tecidos industriais, continua a ser o melhor local da capital para apreciar a diversidade textil do país e apoiar a economia local.
reviews.textTranslated: The Tais Market in Dili is a central hub for the preservation and trade of Timorese culture. It brings together traditional textiles (tais) from various municipalities and handcrafted items, serving as a vital source of income for weavers' cooperatives. Although it faces challenges such as the rise of synthetic materials and industrial fabrics, it remains the best place in the capital to appreciate the country's textile diversity and support the local economy.

Museum tentang perjuangan rakyat Timor-Leste meraih kemerdekaan. Dari era penjajahan Portugis hingga pendudukan Indonesia. Wajib dikunjungi kalau mau belajar sejarah, utamanya hal-hal yang tidak akan diajarkan di sekolah-sekolah di Indonesia.

Saya jadi paham dan memang selayaknya Timor-Leste menjadi negara sendiri dan bukan bagian dari Indonesia.

Museum ini lebih banyak berupa ilustrasi dan teks narasi, dibandingkan benda-benda bernilai historis. Teks dalam 3 bahasa: Tetum, Portugis dan Inggris. Sayangnya tata letak teks bahasa Inggrisnya kurang nyaman, jadi kalau mau membaca kadang harus sambil jongkok atau duduk di lantai.

Ada perpustakaan juga tentang Sejarah timor leste, perjuangannya, maupun tentang Timor-Leste sebagai negara baru.

Sebenarnya ada aturan tidak boleh mengabil foto di dalam Museum, tp saya diam2 ambil foto hehehehe.
reviews.textTranslated:
This museum tells the story of the Timorese people's struggle for independence, from the Portuguese colonial era to the Indonesian occupation. It's a must-visit if you want to learn about history, especially things not taught in Indonesian schools.

I came to understand that Timor-Leste truly deserves to be its own country, not part of Indonesia.

This museum focuses more on illustrations and narrative text than historical objects. The text is in three languages: Tetum, Portuguese, and English. Unfortunately, the layout of the English text is not comfortable, so sometimes you have to squat or sit on the floor to read.

There's also a library about the history of Timor-Leste, its struggle, and Timor-Leste as a new nation.

There's actually a rule against taking photos inside the museum, but I secretly took one, hehehe.

reviews.text:
A museum you must visit when you come to Timor-Leste.
When we talk about genocide, our minds often jump straight to Europe. But traveling through Southeast Asia, I’ve repeatedly come across stories of occupation and genocide from the eastern side of the world—stories that are just as brutal, just as important, and far less spoken about.
Timor-Leste is a newly independent Asian nation that lived through decades of occupation under different regimes. The trauma here runs deep—woven through families, carried across generations. This museum stands as a quiet but powerful reminder of the ugly reality of colonialism, war, and genocide.
What makes the experience truly human, though, are the guides.
The people who walk you through the exhibitions are not just historians—they are witnesses. Many of them lived through the occupation themselves, while also carrying stories passed down from their parents and grandparents. They bridge the gaps between dates, events, and photographs, helping you connect the incidents in a way books never can.
It is a testimony to human endurance and strength—to return every day and tell stories of resistance, loss, and survival. To educate others about the occupation, not as distant history, but as lived reality.
Listening to them, you begin to understand the true gravity of what happened—what was lost, what was endured, and how easily we take life for granted.
And yet… what stays with me the most is the people outside the museum.
Everyone smiles.
They want to know where you’re from.
Their favorite Bollywood movie is Kuch Kuch Hota Hai—and they love talking about it.
There is caution, of course (and that’s understandable). But there is also warmth, curiosity, and resilience.
This country humbles you in ways you don’t expect.
It makes you slow down.
It makes you appreciate what you have.
And for that, I’m truly grateful to be here

특히 전시 중간에 이미지를 볼 수 있는 태블렛이 하나 있는데 꼭 보시길 바란다.
이 작은 나라에서 민족의 자유와 독립을 위해서 힘이 터무니없이 작음을 알면서도 포기하지 않고 투쟁을 이어갔다는 사실이 인상깊었다.
왜 샤나나 구스마오를 그렇게 좋아하는지 알 것 같았다.
reviews.textTranslated:
Admission is $5.

It vividly portrays a history of desperate and heartbreaking resistance, so poignant that it brought tears to my eyes.

In particular, there is a tablet in the middle of the exhibition where you can view images, so I highly recommend checking it out.

I was deeply impressed by the fact that in this small country, they continued the struggle for national freedom and independence without giving up, even while knowing their power was woefully insufficient.

I think I understand why people like Shana and Gusmao so much.

reviews.name: TheWildTian大田真野
reviews.text:
Register and purchase a ticket at the entrance. Tickets are 0.25 for students (including international students), $1 for local adults, and $5 for foreigners.

Photography and videography are not permitted in the exhibition halls, and also food and drinks.

The exhibition is primarily composed of images, all annotated in Portuguese, Tetum, and English, though the font size in the latter two is a bit jarring.

The main exhibition is on the first floor. There are some photos on the second floor, and it seems there was once a cafe in the lobby and balcony. The third floor is empty, just a place for staff to smoke.

The visit lasts 1-2 hours and focuses on the museum's main theme, "The East Timor Struggle." This youngest country in Asia was founded not long ago, and most of its citizens have experienced it firsthand.

The visit is quite somber, allowing us to overcome our grief while also discovering our country's rich culture and resources, especially its ethnic traditions and natural resources.

🎬2025.9.20

reviews.name: Jonty Crane
reviews.text: The first fine arts school, cultural center and artists’ association in Timor-Leste, established in 2003. It gained an international reputation for its varied, and often surreal, art incorporating Timorese culture and motifs. In December 2021 it was controversially evicted from its home in the former National Museum in Comoro, which had been promised by the then government to veterans. Thankfully it found a new home in the former air traffic control tower of the original Dili airport, located to the south of Nicolau Lobato Presidential Palace. It isn’t easy to find, but the Google Maps location is correct, enter through the gates by the storm water channel and turn right. Microlet local buses #3 and #10 and short walk.

reviews.text: 博物馆本身应该是全国最高规格的了，虽然游客屈指可数但值得一来，不过有些小的疏忽和差池，举隅如各个国家对东帝汶问题（Timor-Leste issues）反应的展板上把给印尼总统致信年份打成了1988，当时还是苏哈托专政，就算年份没错，人名也对不上；此外这部分还有春秋笔法，不过整体看来并不算特别严重，只能说美中不足，3$门票还是值的
reviews.textTranslated: The museum itself is probably the highest-standard in the country, and although there are very few visitors, it's worth a visit. However, there are some minor oversights and errors. For example, the display board on the various countries' responses to the Timor-Leste issues incorrectly listed the year of the letter to the Indonesian president as 1988, when Suharto was still in power. Even if the year is correct, the name doesn't match. There are also some instances of misrepresentation in this section. However, overall, these aren't particularly serious issues; they are just minor flaws. The $3 entrance fee is still worthwhile.

reviews.name: Nugroho Saputro
reviews.text:
1. Bekas penjara Balide ini sekarang dijadikan museum. Namanya Centro Nacional Chega!
2. Di sini sempat dijadikan tempat buat menahan dan torture tahanan politik.
3. Untuk masuk ke museum dikenai biaya masuk $2. Terus seperti biasa diminta isi data pengunjung.
4. Pas masuk pertama kali, ada semacam taman yang dipasangi boards yang bertuliskan tentang informasi-informasi mengenai penjara-penjara tempat penahanan tahanan politik. Cukup informatif sih.
5. Masuk ke tengah-tengah, banyak juga informasi mengenai kekerasan-kekerasan yang terjadi di era pendudukan Indonesia di Timor-Leste. Yang menarik ada foto-foto di masa lalu, termasuk ketika Dili dibumihanguskan pasca referendum. Dan pembantaian di sebuah gereja di Suai.
6. Kemudian gw masuk ke satu sudut, dark cells. Ini adalah sudut yang nggak ikut terbakar ketika pembumihangusan pasca referendum. Awalnya gw rada takut masuknya, soalnya vibenya nggak enak.
reviews.textTranslated:
1. The former Balide prison is now a museum. It's called the Centro Nacional Chega!
2. This place was once used to detain and torture political prisoners.
3. There's a $2 entrance fee to enter the museum. As usual, you'll be asked to fill in your visitor details.
4. When you first enter, there's a park with boards displaying information about the prisons where political prisoners were held. It's quite informative.
5. As you move into the center, there's also a lot of information about the violence that occurred during the Indonesian occupation of Timor-Leste. Interestingly, there are photos from the past, including the razing of Dili after the referendum and the massacre at a church in Suai.
6. Then I went into a corner, the dark cells. This is the corner that didn't burn during the post-referendum destruction. At first, I was a little afraid to go in because the vibe was unsettling.

reviews.name: Jonty Crane
reviews.text: The best known hot springs in the country were developed by the Portuguese, with a resort complex built around the pools, but fell into disrepair. In 2016 the whole complex was redeveloped, but little maintenance appears to have taken place since. As of 2024 the toilets are completely out of action, and derelict buildings surround the pools. The hot springs produce ~2,000 litres of water per minute. There are three pools, one very hot (up to ~50C), one hot, and one cold. Despite only being 55km from Dili, allow at least 5 hours to get there, along increasingly bad roads that require good off-road skills.

reviews.text: Cristo Rei Beach is located in East Timor, which is officially known as Timor-Leste. It is the most visited place in the capital city of Díli. People usually go there to swim and hike up Cristo Rei Mountain. At the top of the mountain, there is a massive statue of Jesus. I used to go there with my family, especially to celebrate birthdays. It was the perfect spot because it is the closest beach to the city and to our house in East Timor. There are also local vendors who sell grilled corn. After a long swim, buying a warm grilled corn is the absolute best combination.

A well-maintained stretch of beach, still growing with ongoing development. In the afternoons, the area comes alive—people running, exercising, or simply enjoying a gentle walk along the shore. Near the entrance, local vendors offer fresh coffee, cold drinks, and grilled corn, perfect to enjoy while watching the waves roll in.

We swam at the far end of Cristo Rei Beach, where it’s quieter and more serene.
A scenic path leads you up to the iconic Christ statue, rewarding you with breathtaking views over the city of Dili and the coastline below.

A place where the rhythm of daily life meets the beauty of the sea—peaceful, vibrant, and full of heart.

reviews.text:
Hotel in a part of the world without many, and none that appear on any common booking platforms. Had no problem securing a room for the night as a walk-in around 4pm, after the flight from Dili. Room was $35/night and included breakfast which I wasn’t told/expecting, just found food waiting outside my room when I went to leave around 8am. Seems to cater more to longer stays, staff seemed surprised when I handed over cash for only one night.
Receptionist was friendly, after wandering around to find a hotel I wasn’t in the mood to wander around and find a restaurant open so requested dinner, which the kitchen prepared for $5. A minute’s walk to the waterfront.
Room itself is very basic and not particularly clean. For the location and price I wasn’t expecting much, and the room met that level of expectation. Shower had warm water, two bottles of water provided, bed comfortable enough. Found a large cockroach in the bathroom who was not at all phased by my presence.

reviews.name: Rosana Ear
reviews.text:
Nice hotel in front of the beach, near to Cafe del Mare, the regional office of tourism (ZEEMS building) and Dominican cafe. We got a budget double room at 25 USD, located at the back of the main building, including breakfast, private bathroom and with brand new AC unit. The room is like a motel room with chairs and patio in front. The room is basic but is great: comfortable double bed, clean room, full set of amenities, towel, bathroom with western toilet with a bucket to scoop water, as usual in Timor Leste (no hot water, but weather is hot, so it was not a big deal at all).
They also have 35-45 USD-rooms in the main building with better standard I believe.
The ladies are very nice, they always try to help or answer your questions. We borrowed a clothes dryer for our laundry and could put something in their fridge.

reviews.name: Mario Ara
reviews.text:
When I saw this rating I HAD TO write a review, especially seeing the lack of detail in others.
Stayed in hotel Inur Sakato for 9 days during the completion of a local project. The owner is friendly and helpful. I managed to get laundry done with a smile. The room is large, with its own fridge, old school CRT telly, huge double bed, and personal bathroom. The room is clean although the bathroom could use a bit of work which I happily did myself.
Being a resourceful experienced traveler that realises that I’m in a still developing country, I could have easily given this review 5 stars. Speaking to the locals it is about the best that can be obtained. And it has everything you need. If you are precious then this place may not be for you, but in that case Oecusse is certainly not for you. Enjoy :D

reviews.text: Located some 15 minutes by motorbike from the center of town,  Aosnak is marked by a hill called Pono, there are actually two discernible peaks. According to military maps Pono Stands  60 meters above sea level.  Is a lovely place to go. Beautiful view and lovely beach. Aosnak river mouth is great for Bird-watching and Odanating. There is an old trek from the eastern side of the hill, fairly easy to get to the first peak at more or less 40 meters above sea level.

reviews.text: This is a very easy and nice track. Located some 2 km away from the main road, it is a river bed track, so take proper foot wear. It takes anywhere from 45 - 50 minutes to reach the falls, please be careful not to use the existing galvanized pipes as a support when hiking as the fitting are not very good and you do not want to damage the make shift water supply to the community. Pretty nice place to go for a swim, it is amongst my favorite swimming holes in Pante Macassar. No guide required, follow the river. Little to no place to set up a table or a mat close to the waterfall but small patches of dry areas downstream make for a wonderful escape. Good time to visit - Mar to May

There are some lovely rock outcrops, the most significant of which is known as Fatu Opu (Mango shaped rock). You can cross to Kolomboe bay beach during low tide, during high tide there is a small track that takes you there. In Kolomboe you will see several fishermen houses/outposts.

reviews.text: On a hill behind central Pante Macassar are the remains of the old Fatu-Suba prison and the residence of the Regional Administrator. A statue of the Virgin Mary was added during the Indonesian occupation, to which a pilgrimage takes place every May. Fatu-Suba is a good place to view Pante Macassar below and is a popular place to watch the sunset, though getting a clear view can be challenge. From the waterfront it is a 20-30 minute walk to the top of the hill, along pavement on the flat, and a reasonably steep and rough road up the hillside.

Along with the Waterfalls of Cucute Trail, Nu’uba’u – Fonte Sagrada Trail is the best known hike in the Oé-Cusse region. It follows a river system, from fields of corn to boulder scrambling to reach the attractive Fonte Sagrada waterfall. It is quite an interesting walk, though particularly if done during the wet season, you need to be confident on wet, slippery rocks.

Permission is needed from the local community, along with a $25 payment, to walk the trail. Pay in the house to the left of where the trail starts and a local guide is required, to find one try Nato on +670 7539 4952.

reviews.text:
Spoiler alert: I write the location of the paintings at the bottom.

Highly recommended short hike (10 minutes from the road sign) to a fascinating and historic cave.  Be warned, there is a $10/person charge that ISN'T posted, so if you go on the hike, someone may approach you for money.  We later validated this charge at the Walu guesthouse.  The little hike through the jungle has a few steps, but about as challenging as a staircase.  The path was fairly obvious.  The cave itself is deeper and grander than I expected.  To explore, bring a bright flashlight.  Yes, there are bats (harmless), but they are high above.

There were many cave drawings at the entrance of the cave.  The drawings are high up, but visible in natural light.  A bright flashlight is recommended to see in better detail.  You'll see suns, stick figures, and geometric shapes.  The sign at the road describes what some of them mean.

If you've come this far in Timor for Jaco island, take an hour or two for this site.  It's great and unique.

reviews.name: Jose Felix
reviews.text: Ilha desabitada no topo leste da ilha. Depois de chegar a Tutuala, que não é fácil atendendo ao estado de degradação das estradas. Fazer a descida até ao canal que separa timor-leste da ilha de jaco, agora alcatrão, outrora em terra batida, são 8km de expectativa de obter com êxito a travessia do canal, nem sempre fiável pelas condições do estado do mar. A travessia é assegurada por pescadores disponíveis, mediante um preço de $10 dólares por pessoa. O almoço, pode ser negociado com o pescador, porque, na travessia sempre se arranja um peixe para a refeição. A pernoita na ilha está proibida. O snorkeling é permitido e o protetor solar é recomendado.  As águas tépidas e azuis de capa de revista, não dão descanso ao corpo, pois estar na água é mais que obrigatório. Está, é uma das experiências a não perder por quem passa em Timor-leste, um pouco desgastante, verdade, mas vale apena. A não perder.
reviews.textTranslated: An uninhabited island at the easternmost tip of the island. After reaching Tutuala, which isn't easy due to the poor state of the roads, the descent to the channel separating East Timor from Jaco Island—now paved, once a dirt track—is an 8km journey with the expectation of successfully crossing the channel, though this isn't always reliable due to sea conditions. The crossing is provided by willing fishermen for $10 per person. Lunch can be negotiated with the fisherman, as you can always find fish for your meal during the crossing. Overnight stays on the island are prohibited. Snorkeling is allowed, and sunscreen is recommended. The warm, blue waters, picture-perfect, offer no rest, as being in the water is more than obligatory. This is one of the experiences not to be missed by anyone visiting East Timor; a little tiring, admittedly, but worthwhile. Don't miss it.

Drone View Perspective - ©Lélio Alves

reviews.name: aj
reviews.text: Jaco Island, located off the eastern coast of Timor-Leste, is a pristine tropical haven that enchants visitors with its untouched beauty. Accessible only by boat, the island is a sanctuary of powdery white sands surrounded by turquoise waters, creating a postcard-perfect setting. Snorkelers and divers revel in the vibrant coral reefs, encountering an array of marine life beneath the crystalline surface. With no permanent inhabitants and limited infrastructure, Jaco offers a serene escape for those seeking tranquility. Its unspoiled landscapes, coupled with the warm hospitality of locals, make Jaco Island a true paradise for nature enthusiasts and adventurers alike.

​A haunting but essential stop if you want to understand the history of Laga. This building was originally a Portuguese administrative office, but it has a dark past from 1976–1980 when it was used as a military post and detention center. You can still see Indonesian military insignias and bullet holes scarring the walls.

​Important Safety Warning:
If you decide to explore, please be extremely careful. The structure is in ruins and the rooftop is heavily damaged and infested with termites—it doesn't look stable.

reviews.name: Jonty Crane
reviews.text: Lake Ira Lalaro is the largest lake in Timor-Leste. It is a seasonal body of water, whose size expands greatly during the wet season, from 1,000 hectares to 5,500 hectares. The northern shore is flat grassland that reclaims much of the lake during the dry season, while the southern shore is swampy with half drowned trees, more photogenic but harder to reach. It is hard is really appreciate the lake without using a drone as the landscape is so flat. The lake is apparently home to around 300 crocodiles, so be careful! Note that the road around the southern shore of the lake to Jaco Island is only passable by motorbike, and then only if you are comfortable driving over a rudimentary wooden bridge.

reviews.name: John Dooley
reviews.text: This is a location where a fruit bat/flying fox colony resides. It is adjacent to some regular houses in a village, and access is via the road on the left of the Gariurai Primary School on the main road. Bit tricky to find but I'm sure people could point the way if you made some sufficient bat-like gestures. My friend is a professional guide and told me this is the only such bat colony in Timor-Leste. The bats seem pretty similar to those found in Australia, no doubt related to them, but I noticed that unlike colonies in Australia these ones didn't smell. That's a welcome bit of evolutionary progress, certainly. The bats are easy to see and as usual are semi-active at day time, and at sunset they take off across the area.

reviews.name: Buren
reviews.text:
Disclaimer: My trip was not current.

We stopped by Pousada de Maubisse for a lunch break on our way up to Mount Ramelau or Tatamailau (local language means Grandfather of all) is the highest mountain in Timor Leste and also Timor Island. It is a rest house located in Maubisse, which is the pass over before going to Hato Bulico where we would start our climb. It could be an option for staying overnight if you want to spend more time exploring Maubisse at that time, currently I believe it's under renovation.

It was a tranquil experience for us as no one was around. When we entered the place, there were two rows of rooms on both sides. After that we would pass by a garden with surrounding 360 view before we entered the big house. There was a rustic fire place in the living room, or maybe more suitable to be called dining room. The place was empty and cold when no one was around. The fire place was nice; the whole space was spacious but quite old. We saw a sitting room with two stretch of long sofa, there was a clean toilet with full big bucket of water and a lot of toilet papers.

The food was simple and good, but took very long to prepare. On our way back from the climbing the next day, we ordered before we started the descent and yet we needed to wait for another two hours. I assumed they cooked with fire wood that was why it took much longer but it was good.

It's very nice climb overall and the stopover at Pousada de Maubisse is very memorable. We had the place all for ourselves and it's a nice, quiet, gorgeous, and peaceful time there.

reviews.name: Ari Wekku Sääski
reviews.text: Maubisse is full of history to learn and study. 2018 I was filming Timor Awakening 7, Australian War Veteran group was travelling with Ian Hampel, WW2 Commando who was observing Japanese movements 1942 all over Timor-Leste. Amazing story of hardship and survival. I was honoured to spend time with this amazing person. His memories were sharp as knife. Large group of TA7 group was following the paths Ian Hampel walked through Timor-Leste. Postu Maubisse was strategically important spot for Japanese and they stationed lots of troops there. Australian Commandos were observing their movements from the surrounding hills and relayed the information to Australia. Many fights occurred in this area and Commandos disappeared to the mountains with the help of Timorese. Japanese never catched these "White Ghosts".

reviews.text:
"Larigutu Viqueque Ossu" refers to locations within the Viqueque Municipality of Timor-Leste, specifically highlighting Larigutu and Ossu, which are administrative areas within the larger Viqueque region.
Here's a breakdown of what the information indicates about these places:
Viqueque Municipality:
* Location: Located in the southeast of Timor-Leste, about 183 km from Dili, the capital. It borders Lautém (east), the Timor Sea (south), Manatuto (west), and Baucau (north).
* Administrative Posts: It comprises five administrative posts: Lacluta, Ossu, Uatu-Lari (also known as Leça or Watulari), Uatu-Carbau (Watucarbau), and Viqueque, which collectively contain 36 villages (sucos).
* History: Viqueque had traditional authority before Portuguese rule. The Portuguese established their office in 1698 and in 1859, Viqueque became a district known as Bibiluto District. It was a district during the Indonesian occupation and became a municipality after independence.

From Cristo Rei beach you can climb the stairs halfway to Cristo Rei statue and then head down to Dolok Oan or you can take the road around (by going up on the roundabout). If you are looking for a more peaceful and quiet day, I would recommend going to Dolok Oan on a weekday as it is usually crowded on Sundays and public holidays. Also I recommend bringing your own food and drinks as there are no restaurants or convenience stores nearby (although one or two peddlers might be around selling oranges, banana, or even peanuts).

reviews.name: James Howard
reviews.text:
When Timor Leste was occupied by Indonesia, this beach was known as "Pantai pasir putih" in Bahasa Indonesia, or "White sand beach". The name is appropriate - although not particularly imaginative - as the beach is covered in white sand!

When I visited, some 23 years ago, the beach was quite eerie. It was deserted, apart from myself, and there were little concrete picnic shelters dotted along the beach that were slowly filling with drifting sand or become overgrown with trees. There were also some old, decrepit "pedalo" boats, little boats that you can pedal in calm water, that were half-buried in the sand. Clearly, the shelters and pedal-boats dated from the 1970s, some twenty years earlier, when East Timor was a Portuguese colony and a popular destination for Portuguese holiday-makers.

It would be interesting to know if any of the old, decrepit concrete picnic shelters, or any other trace of its old history, still remain.

reviews.text: To situate you before you go below the water's surface, the Christo Rei East beach is only about 20 minutes from Dili by car.  You have to drive over the ridge and turn back on a coastal road to reach it.  Because it is a bit farther than the more common Christo Rei beach, it is much less crowded and sometimes you get the whole beach to yourself.  For divers, the entry is very gradual on sandy bottom covered in sea grass where you may encounter seahorses if you are lucky (see Charlie the seahorse below).  The area is covered in giant clams in many colors and the reefs harbor lots of cool critters. #scubadiving

reviews.name: Jonty Crane
reviews.text:
Should be visited with a local guide (which your accommodation should be able to arrange), as it is a sacred place and is unmarked from the main road. Ili Kere Kere is $10 per person.

Ili Kere Kere is reached by a rough road off the main road between Tutuala and Valu Beach, followed by a 2.3km return walk (not the 250m denoted by the signage at the start of the trail). This walk gets increasingly rough and steep (downhill) before reaching the best known rock art depicting a sea urchin, as well as a harder to recognise image of cockfighting. Walking around the base of the cliff offers great views of Jaco Island in the distance. Allow about an hour to visit Ili Kere Kere. Look out for the giant bee hives hanging from the rock overhang above the rock art.

From where the trail to Ili Kere Kere starts there are two other trails that are far less visited. Pati-Patinu (500m walk apparently) goes to seven holes in stone, which demonstrate a tradition practice by ancestors of the Tutuala area. Moa Mimiraka (700m walk) is home to four pieces of rock art illustrating headhunting, arm stencil, a festive event, and warriors.

reviews.name: Liam Bushrod
reviews.text: A beautiful stay situated in the middle of a  local community downhill from the old town. It’s quiet and peaceful and everything has been built from the ground up. The staff are lovely, food is awesome and there’s loads of beds. Hostelworld said there was only one bed available but when we turned up, there was only one other person booked in to stay that night. US$15 per person per night, including breakfast. The beach is a 15 minute walk down the road. Would very happily come back!

reviews.name: Martin LR
reviews.text:
J’ai demandé le prix par whatsapp. Pour un bungalow, le monsieur me dit 50$ pour 2.
Je suis étonné car sur booking.com, c’est 25$ pour deux. Je lui fait remarquer. Il dit que c’est une erreur, que c’est que pour une personne. Or, je fais la réservation booking. C’est bien indiqué 25$ pour 2 personnes. Il essaye donc de nous arnaquer. Ensuite, il me dit « ok, pour 25$ », mais supprime ta réservation et paye nous directement, sans passer par booking. Je suis d’accord, fais une demande d’annulation.
Finalement, à cause d’un problème de scooter nous sommes bloqués à Dili et ne pouvons pas y aller. Il refuse l’annulation booking.
En sommet : tentative d’arnaque et malhonnêteté. Essayer d’arnaquer les touristes ne fera pas venir davantage de gens.
reviews.textTranslated:
I asked for the price via WhatsApp. For a bungalow, the man told me $50 for two people.
I was surprised because on Booking.com, it's $25 for two. I pointed this out to him. He said it was a mistake, that it was only for one person. However, I made the booking on Booking.com. It clearly stated $25 for two people. So he was trying to scam us. Then he told me, "Okay, for $25," but cancel your reservation and pay us directly, without going through Booking.com. I agreed and requested a cancellation.
Finally, due to a problem with the scooter, we were stuck in Dili and couldn't go. He refused the Booking.com cancellation.
In short: attempted scam and dishonesty. Trying to scam tourists won't bring more people.

A acomodação é excelente e irrepreensivelmente limpa. Lá fora, o verde envolve tudo e convida a respirar fundo. A comida é extraordinária, fresca, simples e cheia de sabor, como se viesse diretamente da terra para o prato. Um lugar que nos reconecta com o essencial e nos lembra como é bom viver devagar.
reviews.textTranslated: Paradise on Earth. You sleep in a silence that soothes you from within, you wake up to the light slowly entering and the feeling that time slows down. The accommodation is excellent and impeccably clean. Outside, greenery envelops everything and invites you to take a deep breath. The food is extraordinary, fresh, simple and full of flavor, as if it came directly from the earth to the plate. A place that reconnects us with the essential and reminds us how good it is to live slowly.

reviews.name: Zineb Homman Loudiye
reviews.text: The most beautiful of all Da Terras so far! It's green with views over rice fields and the sea from the elevated platform and some of the bungalows. There's a good atmosphere because as soon as you enter, you can hear the ladies singing in the kitchen, which brings a bit of pep. Dorms were comfortable, each with mosquito nets and fans, and the open bathrooms were super cool. The nice beach/tree arch is about a 30min walk down and the Wai-usu fresh spring about a 20min walk up. The Old Town of Baucau is about 40min away by walk, if there are no microlets (50 centavos Diwake-Old Town / $1 Diwake-New Town). It gets hot and steep, but it's doable and you can cool off at the public pool or spring on the way. Plus they organise whale watching tours for $45 (don't forget to bring mask + snorkel from the hostel!). Many thanks to Eta for running the show while I was there 🫰

reviews.name: Liza Chang
reviews.text:
My first visit here was last July, and knew that it’s also possible to go whale watching here! So I made sure to come back this time. I was welcomed, as always, with their homemade kombucha upon arrival—it’s just as refreshing and tasty as I remembered.

This time we stayed for two nights, one in the dorm and one in the Blue Room. Both were simple but comfortable, with fans and plenty of power outlets. I love the natural scent from the dried leaves used for the roof because it feels so close to nature. I especially loved the open roof toilet. It is such a unique experience that made me feel immersed in the outdoors.

Breakfast with homemade bread, marmalade, and Timor coffee. Meals can be arranged in advance, and every dish is freshly cooked, I liked grilled fish a lot.

All guests staying there joined whale watching trips for first day and made it for two days eventually. It was great going with local fishing boats that move gently with smaller engines. The fishermen were very professional at spotting whales and keeping a respectful distance. We spotted sperm whales, with four boats joining the expedition. It was truly unforgettable.
reviews.responseFromOwnerText:
Dear Liza,
Thank you so much for your great review! It will help other guests to understand a bit more about our projects!
Warm regards

After drinking we were told they would cost 3.5 each for skinny can of tonic. That’s an outrageous price. Not a good experience.

reviews.name: Ricardo Antunes
reviews.text:
Apesar de já conhecer o Fernando Madeira há vários anos, nunca tinha tido a oportunidade de visitar o espaço daTerra em Baucau.
Desta vez proporcionou-se e foi uma experiência muito boa. Fiquei, com os meus 3 filhos, num bungalow para 4 pessoas.

Decidimos ficar duas noites, a caminho entre Díli e a ponta leste da ilha (onde fomos visitar Jaco). É uma excelente opção, para tornar esse trajeto mais fácil (de Dili a Baucau são 2 horas de carro, com a estrada toda em muito boas condições).

O alojamento, a comida e o serviço são fantásticos. O acesso pode ser um bocadinho complicado dependendo do tipo de carro que se use (um carro citadino terá alguma dificuldade em aceder à última parte do percurso), mas em geral só temos a dizer bem.

Todo o conceito é de quinta ecológica, inserida no meio da natureza, mas muito bem ajustada ao conforto de quem quer descansar e usufruir de uns dias em paz.

As casa de banho são comunitárias, mas há várias e com um nível de conforto que eu não imaginava sequer encontrar ali.

Muito bom!
reviews.textTranslated:
Although I've known Fernando Madeira for several years, I'd never had the opportunity to visit daTerra in Baucau.

This time it was possible, and it was a very good experience. I stayed with my 3 children in a bungalow for 4 people.

We decided to stay two nights, on our way between Dili and the eastern tip of the island (where we went to visit Jaco). It's an excellent option to make that journey easier (from Dili to Baucau it's a 2-hour drive, with the road in very good condition).

The accommodation, food, and service are fantastic. Access can be a little tricky depending on the type of car you use (a city car will have some difficulty accessing the last part of the route), but overall we only have good things to say.

The whole concept is that of an ecological farm, nestled in nature, but very well suited to the comfort of those who want to relax and enjoy a few peaceful days.

The bathrooms are communal, but there are several, and with a level of comfort that I didn't even imagine finding there.

Very good!
reviews.responseFromOwnerText:
Caro Ricardo,
Muito agradecido pela detalhada descrição que certamente ajudará novos hóspedes a "descobrirem" o projecto daTerra em Baucau.

Os carros pequenos podem estacionar no centro de saúde ou na casa da professora Zélia, 3 minutos a pé da quinta. 

É com muita gratidão que a equipa daTerra recebe o teu comentário e dá-nos motivação para continuar a melhorar o espaço!
Abraço grande!

reviewContext.Rooms: O espaço tem Bungalows com várias tipologias. Nós ficámos um  para 4 pessoas (colchão e mosquiteiro).
reviewContext.Nearby activities: Baucau tem vários pontos de atração. É uma cidade antiga, , com muita água e verde. Desde destaca-se logo o centro da vila, a Pousada de Baucau (onde se come muito bem - destaque para o leite creme), ou o antigo Mercado. Depois há a piscina pública (perto da Pousada) e a praia. Mais afastado, há Venilale ou Baguia, que também merecem uma visita.
reviewContext.Safety: O espaço daTerra fica inserido na comunidade e os vizinhos são muito amigáveis. Todo o espaço é vedado, para maior proteção.
reviewContext.Food & drinks: O daTerra disponibiliza o pequeno-almoço e refeições. Frequentemente tem peixe fresco. É conveniente marcar as refeições com antecedência.

reviews.name: Constança Teixeira
reviews.text: A must-have experience in Timor-Leste! daTerra is exactly what it looks like and more: an eco-lodge, beautifully preserved, with a boho-hippie aesthetic, surrounded by cute vegetable gardens, fire-pits and wooden cabins. You sleep wonderfully in the woods absorbed by the piece and quiet and, of course, with a full-belly by the amazing cooks Mana Eta and Mana Fitri (definitely recommend their moringa butter, grilled chicken, kombucha and passion-fruit gin!). Baucau has a special mystique and daTerra plays a huge role in it :)

É possível visitar e sentar com calma para beber um café expresso ou um café Timor.
Para almoçar é possível encomendar um prato de carne, peixe grelhado ou vegetariano.
Eu que não sou vegetariana, almocei vegetariano e não sobrou nada.
O Fernando é uma pessoa muito especial e a sua equipa é maravilhosa.

It's a magical space completely immersed in nature, with great ecological concerns.
It's possible to visit and sit calmly to drink an espresso or a Timor coffee.
For lunch, you can order a meat dish, grilled fish, or a vegetarian option.
Even though I'm not a vegetarian, I had a vegetarian lunch and there wasn't a single bite left.
Fernando is a very special person and his team is wonderful.

Friendly conversation with local community will lead to an offer to show you the path, which is highly recommended. The walk through Rice Paddies is spectacular. The natural bridge feature is a long ancient tunnel of about 40metres in length in a tall rocky chasm, forming one iridescent aqua river, with cliffs and jungle above. reviews.name: Falentino Bento
reviews.text:
Mundu Perdido, meaning "Lost World" in Portuguese, is a significant mountain and a protected area located in the Viqueque District of Timor-Leste, specifically to the west of the town of Ossu.
Here's a detailed explanation:
Name Origin: The name "Mundu Perdido" comes from the Portuguese, likely given because the mountain is frequently shrouded in mist and clouds, making it appear as if it's hidden or "lost." This phenomenon is common for many mountains in Timor-Leste during much of the year.

reviews.name: Silvio Alves
reviews.text: Fatin Furak

reviews.name: Jonty Crane
reviews.text: The landscapes of Mundo Perdido ("Lost World" in Portuguese) are varied and atmospheric places to explore on foot. The Portuguese called it the Lost World as the area is so often hidden in mist. The best time of year to visit to try and get views is between August and October. The area was an important hideout for Timorese independence fighters during the Indonesian occupation. Now it is designated an ‘Important Bird Area’, home to 63 different species, and is one of the three most important areas for orchids in Timor-Leste. There are no clear trails and getting lost is easily done, so a local guide is strongly recommended. A couple of options are Joni on +670 7727 7996 or M.Xisto on +670 7604 1207. Two popular places to start hiking from are about 45 minutes drive (on a challenging road) to the west of Larigutu and from close to Ossu.

title: Cristo Rei Beach
description: This narrow, sandy beach offers swimming, sunbathing & views of the famous Cristo Rei statue.

reviews.name: Andrea Pereira
reviews.text:
Um lugar especial que merece ser melhor preservado

O Cristo Rei de Díli é muito mais do que um miradouro: é um local de oração, contemplação, contacto com a natureza e um espaço onde muitos fazem a caminhada diária para cuidar da saúde ou simplesmente sentir-se mais perto do céu.
É, por isso, triste encontrar lixo abandonado ao longo do percurso e nas áreas envolventes. Seria importante que todos, visitantes e comunidade local, cuidassem melhor deste espaço, e que as entidades responsáveis reforçassem a sua preservação e limpeza. Um lugar com tanto significado merece ser mantido limpo, digno e acolhedor para as gerações presentes e futuras.
reviews.textTranslated:
A special place that deserves to be better preserved

The Cristo Rei statue in Dili is much more than a viewpoint: it is a place of prayer, contemplation, contact with nature, and a space where many take their daily walk to take care of their health or simply feel closer to heaven.

It is, therefore, sad to find litter abandoned along the route and in the surrounding areas. It would be important for everyone, visitors and the local community, to take better care of this space, and for the responsible entities to reinforce its preservation and cleaning. A place with so much meaning deserves to be kept clean, dignified, and welcoming for present and future generations.

reviews.name: Natali Pearson
reviews.text: Others have written about the history of this site. I’m here to share just how little of the wreck remains in situ. Even since 2022, the site has changed significantly, with large pieces either missing or below the sand. I visited 20 August 2026, and have shared those photos here; four days later I went back at lowest possible tide and the sand had shifted so much that nothing was visible. A good lesson in coastal morphology and intertidal shipwrecks. Also be warned - the large rusty-orange circular object on the beach has nothing to do with the wreck - it’s an old buoy.

reviews.name: Michael Stone
reviews.text:
HMAS Voyager (D31/I31) (formerly HMS Voyager (G36/G16/D31)) was a W-class destroyer of the Royal Navy (RN) and Royal Australian Navy (RAN). Commissioned into the RN in 1918, the destroyer remained in RN service until 1933, when she was transferred to the RAN. Recommissioned, Voyager served in the Mediterranean and Pacific theatres of World War II until 23 September 1942, when she ran aground while trying to deliver troops to Timor. The ship was damaged by Japanese bombers while trying to refloat, then was scuttled by her crew.

reviews.name: Jonty Crane
reviews.text: One of the best known beaches in Timor-Leste. It was a popular spot with UN peacekeepers during the early 2000s. Locals would charge them $1 to access the beach. Entry is now free but the beach is closed with the gate locked and facilities (toilets, pools, etc) out of action. There is no timeline for when the beach will reopen, but it can be accessed by walking around the walls by the beach. The towers are a novel feature, offering good views and shade, but along with the barbed wire topped perimeter wall, make it feel more like a prison camp than a beachside resort. There is good snorkelling here. The beach is part of the large Subaun Important Bird Area which stretches for ~60,000 acres to Mt Curi.

reviews.name: KB
reviews.text:
Discover Rai Mutin (White Land), one of Timor-Leste's geological wonders. This unique landscape features expansive areas of exposed white limestone, created by the weathering of the rock's top surface. The result is a striking, foreign environment that contrasts dramatically with the surrounding green hills.

While several areas of 'white land' can be found throughout the Aileu district, this particular site is one of the most prominent and accessible formations. Located just a 15-minute drive from Aileu's main town, Rai Mutin Limestone Park offers a free-to-enter natural experience. It's an ideal spot for photography, a short walk, or simply to appreciate a quieter side of Aileu.

reviews.name: Alex Gundry
reviews.text:
A pretty impressive collection of stories of a people who were forced into revealing their bravery, against an invading Indonesian militia that used brutality and deception to enslave a small peaceful country. The reporters were stuck out of their depth, but tried to inform the world of the tragedy; paying with their lives.
This museum, like many others, stands patiently to tell these stories.

reviews.text: Easily the best museum in Timor-Leste in terms of the quality of its displays - including a number of photographs that I have never seen before - and the accuracy of its English language descriptions. Obviously less informative overall than the Resistance Museum in Dili, but it provides a detailed summary of Balibo-specific and general Timorese history that is well worth reading, and takes around two hours to visit if you make the effort to read all of the information presented.

reviews.text: Description: Stayed at Ocean View Beach Hotel with a group of 5 friends for 9 days and 8 nights. Did a totally of 17 dives (a mixed of shore, boat and night dives) and a couple more whales + dolphin diving with Aquatica. All our meals were prepared by the hotel's restaurant, where we dined next to the sea.||Food: The food was definitely one of the highlights of the trip! Every meal genuinely wowed me - starting from the appetiser to the main course and finally finishing off with dessert - it was chef's kiss. I feel very blessed every day. While there were some dishes I preferred more than others, overall, it was a truly great and filling experience. We were never left hungry by the end of any meal.. ||Accommodation: As a group of 5, we booked two rooms. Three of us stayed in the Deluxe Room, while the other two stayed in a Standard Cabin. The Standard Cabin was pretty good - definitely better in person than in photos. The space was clean, bright, with strong air conditioning, and it had a nice shower and living area. Unfortunately, the Deluxe Room fell short of our expectations. The photos on the website didn’t match the room we were assigned, so we were a bit disappointed. However, the host offered to swap us to a Standard Cabin after our first night, but we decided to stay. We noticed the staff had cleaned the room better after the first night, and we also preferred the larger living room space, which made it easier for our friends to hang out.||Service: Uncle Danny, the owner of the hotel, always made time for his guests. He would drop by to say hello and share stories that were truly inspiring, making us feel very welcome and at home. All the staff were attentive and friendly, responding to every request with a smile and even remembering our dining preferences. Once we picked a table we liked, they always did their best to reserve that spot for us. In another instance, we requested a specific type of dipping sauce, and almost every meal after that, it was automatically prepared for us during dinner. These small gestures made our experience even more special.||Activities: We spent most of our trip scuba diving with Aquatica, a dive center located at the hotel. Marco and Juve were our main dive guides, and they were quick to spot all the unique marine wildlife at each dive site. We saw many nudibranchs (including Shaun the Sheep), had close encounters with two famous local dugongs, and spotted giant lobsters, octopuses, schools of barracuda, and more. As one of the least experienced divers in the group, I always felt safe and well taken care of by Marco. He also helped us get close and photograph the marine wildlife, which would have been challenging for an inexperienced underwater photographer like myself. Desmond, another dive guide who also runs Aquatica, was fantastic in getting us up close to the pilot whales and spinner dolphins. Desmond was friendly, sociable, and attentive. When he noticed I had a bad sunburn, he quickly grabbed a curved gel ice pack with a thin cloth for me to cool off the burns.||------||TLDR: Although the Deluxe Room fell short of our expectations, it didn’t affect my love for this place. The rich marine wildlife and coral reefs, the delicious heartwarming meals, the hospitality of the staff and hosts, and the relaxing sea breeze and views make this place a must-visit.

reviews.name: Ai Ling Ng
reviews.text:
Stayed at Ocean View Beach Hotel with a group of 5 friends for 9 days and 8 nights. Did a totally of 17 dives (a mixed of shore, boat and night dives) and a couple more whales + dolphin diving with Aquatica. All our meals were prepared by the hotel's restaurant, where we dined next to the sea.

Although the Deluxe Room fell short of our expectations, it didn’t affect my love for this place. The rich marine wildlife and coral reefs, the delicious heartwarming meals, the hospitality of the staff and hosts, and the relaxing sea breeze and views make this place a must-visit.

reviewContext.Rooms: As a group of 5, we booked two rooms. Three of us stayed in the Deluxe Room, while the other two stayed in a Standard Cabin. The Standard Cabin was pretty good - definitely better in person than in photos. The space was clean, bright, with strong air conditioning, and it had a nice shower and living area. Unfortunately, the Deluxe Room fell short of our expectations. The photos on the website didn’t match the room we were assigned, so we were a bit disappointed. However, the host offered to swap us to a Standard Cabin after our first night, but we decided to stay. We noticed the staff had cleaned the room better after the first night, and we also preferred the larger living room space, which made it easier for our friends to hang out.
reviewContext.Nearby activities: We spent most of our trip scuba diving with Aquatica, a dive center located at the hotel. Marco and Juve were our main dive guides, and they were quick to spot all the unique marine wildlife at each dive site. We saw many nudibranchs (including Shaun the Sheep), had close encounters with two famous local dugongs, and spotted giant lobsters, octopuses, schools of barracuda, and more. As one of the least experienced divers in the group, I always felt safe and well taken care of by Marco. He also helped us get close and photograph the marine wildlife, which would have been challenging for an inexperienced underwater photographer like myself. Desmond, another dive guide who also runs Aquatica, was fantastic in getting us up close to the pilot whales and spinner dolphins. Desmond was friendly, sociable, and attentive. When he noticed I had a bad sunburn, he quickly grabbed a curved gel ice pack with a thin cloth for me to cool off the burns.
reviewContext.Food & drinks: The food was definitely one of the highlights of the trip! Every meal genuinely wowed me - starting from the appetiser to the main course and finally finishing off with dessert - it was chef's kiss. I feel very blessed every day. While there were some dishes I preferred more than others, overall, it was a truly great and filling experience. We were never left hungry by the end of any meal..
reviewContext.Noteworthy details: Uncle Danny, the owner of the hotel, always made time for his guests. He would drop by to say hello and share stories that were truly inspiring, making us feel very welcome and at home. All the staff were attentive and friendly, responding to every request with a smile and even remembering our dining preferences. Once we picked a table we liked, they always did their best to reserve that spot for us. In another instance, we requested a specific type of dipping sauce, and almost every meal after that, it was automatically prepared for us during dinner. These small gestures made our experience even more special.

reviews.text: This remarkable boutique eco hotel is nestled in the picturesque mountains of Balibo. ||Views to the ocean and horizon are truly magical at sunset and are enjoyed by locals and travellers alike.  ||Connect with people from across Timor and  around the globe at the Fort Hotel’s restaurant. Fresh local ingredients underpin Timorese inspired dishes. ||Rooms are very comfortable. The staff are caring and friendly. ||There are many things to do in and around Balibo. Hire a bike or take a cultural tour with social enterprise Balibo Trails. Visit the Veterans Museum, the memorial to the Balibo 5, see local weavers, visit the market, hike to the waterfall, sip a G&T around the hotel’s glorious infinity pool.

reviews.name: cherrellp2014
reviews.text: When the mist comes in, the Balibo Fort Hotel seems to float in the clouds.  It reminds me of the Cameron Highlands in the 1960’s when there was no pollution and a trip to the mountain resort was the perfect place to get away from the tropical heat. Built as a Fort 400 years ago by the Portuguese, the original stone walls, entry archway and cannons are still there.  The cannons were part of the Fort’s original defensive design, used to protect the border area between Portuguese Timor and Dutch-controlled territory. Panoramic views from the mountains to the sea, lovely rooms & an infinity pool complete the luxury.|There’s also a Veterans’ Museum in the grounds, that  shares the history of those who have served in Timor-Leste, including  World War II, the Resistance period, INTERFET, and the International Stabilisation Force.  The Hotel is next to the home of the Balibo 5, the 5 Australian journalists killed by invading forces in 1975.

Incrivel Hotel situado nas montanhas de Timor, estilo colonial, muito bonito e confortável! Um serviço  muito cuidadoso e amável. Fomos muito bem recebidos. O Hotel tem uma localização  incrivel com uma vista sobre as montanhas até ao mar. As zonas de estar e a piscina são  muito agradáveis.
Jantámos muito bem, tudo cozinhado no local. Serviram um pequeno almoço maravilhoso no dia seguinte. Gostava de realçar a simpatia e gentileza com que nos receberam, uma amostra da simpatia de todo o Povo Timorense.
Nunca imaginamos que depois de um caminho dificil para aqui chegar iriamos ter toda esta experiência, perdido no meio das montanhas está este Oásis, muito bonito confortável e ao mesmo tempo simples e verdadeiro. A quem visita Timor diria que vir a ao Forte de Balibó é necessario para compreender a realidade deste povo., que se vai entendendo melhor à  medida que nos afastamos de Dili e vamos passando pelas diferentes aldeias e lugares até  aqui chegar.
Nao sei se alguma vez mais voltarei ao Forte Balibó, mas nunca  esquecerei estes dias!
Até sempre
reviews.textTranslated:
Incredible hotel located in the mountains of Timor, colonial style, very beautiful and comfortable! Very attentive and kind service. We were very well received. The hotel has an incredible location with a view over the mountains to the sea. The living areas and the pool are very pleasant.
We had a very good dinner, everything cooked on site. They served a wonderful breakfast the next day. I would like to highlight the friendliness and kindness with which they received us, a sample of the friendliness of all the Timorese people.
We never imagined that after a difficult journey to get here we would have this whole experience, lost in the middle of the mountains is this oasis, very beautiful, comfortable and at the same time simple and true. To anyone visiting Timor I would say that coming to the Balibó Fort is necessary to understand the reality of these people, which is better understood as we move away from Dili and pass through the different villages and places until we get here.
I don't know if I will ever return to the Balibó Fort, but I will never forget these days!
Until next time

reviews.name: Flora Caramella
reviews.text:
A Magical Stay at Balibo Fort Hotel: A Birthday & Anniversary to Remember

My husband and I recently had the most incredible experience at Balibo Fort Hotel, celebrating both my birthday and our first wedding anniversary. Under the new management of Pelikan Paradise, the hotel has truly elevated its hospitality, making our stay absolutely unforgettable.

The villa prepared for us was stunning, offering a perfect blend of comfort, charm, and a breathtaking atmosphere. One of the most memorable highlights was the romantic candlelight dinner in the garden, beautifully set up with twinkling lights and a cozy bonfire. The ambiance was intimate and magical, making our celebration feel incredibly special.

We had brought our own raw ingredients for a cheese and charcuterie plate, and to our delight, Erin, the incredible manager, offered to prepare it beautifully for us. It was such a thoughtful gesture that added an extra touch of elegance to our evening. The in-house birthday cake was another delightful surprise, not only beautifully presented but also absolutely delicious!

Another highlight of our stay was the immaculate pool—so clean and well-maintained that I didn’t want to get out, even when it started raining! Having the entire pool to myself made for an incredibly serene and relaxing experience.

A special thank you to Manager Erin from Malaysia, who went above and beyond in organizing every detail to perfection. Her warmth, attentiveness, and genuine hospitality made our stay truly unforgettable. We are deeply grateful for the effort she and the entire Balibo Fort Hotel team, now managed by Pelikan Paradise, put into making our celebration so special.

If you’re looking for a place that combines history, beauty, and world-class hospitality, Balibo Fort Hotel is a must-visit. We will cherish these memories forever and can’t wait to return!

Highly Recommended!

With gratitude,
Kivo & Flora

reviews.name: KB
reviews.text:
This large tree in Railaco is a remarkable natural apiary, hosting over 20 beehives. The local community has been harvesting honey from this tree annually.

The bees here are a distinctive local species, noted for their black coloration and wasp-like appearance. They are generally calm but can become aggressive if provoked, so visitors are advised to observe quietly from a safe distance.

The honey produced has a unique flavor profile: initially sweet with a distinct, subtle fermented finish that reflects the diverse local flora.

Please support the locals by buying their local honey. Inquire with villagers to find out how you can buy a jar of this sweet product directly from the source.

reviews.text: A beautiful small beach, located about 15 kms east of Dili on the main road to Baucau/ Lautem. reviews.name: Charles Tan
reviews.text: Timor Leste is very untouched. It is here in this country that you almost almost have the beach to yourself. Due to the lack of tourist visiting this country almost every beach is quiet, serene and beautiful. Hera beach is about 30 mins drive from Dili, if you use the hill road passing Becora, you will pass hills and vegetable farms along the way. If you use the seaside road towards Cristo Rei, the view of the sea is breathtaking. The road leads past hills above the beaches. There are some fishermen in Hera beach and sunset is beautiful here.

reviews.name: John Dooley
reviews.text:
This is not the most picturesque beach in the world but lovely and clean for a nice swim, the water is very warm.
When I visited in April 2022, there was no sand in the water, it was a shelf of rock underneath but no dangerous cracks or sharp coral. There were no vendors here at this time but there is a shop at the main intersection.
The entrance to the beach is not obvious from the road, but can be accessed past any of the adjacent buildings on the road (see picture).
There was once an Australian shipwreck here, some local policemen on the beach told me it was no longer visible.

reviews.name: Jonty Crane
reviews.text: Probably the most spectacular waterfall in Timor-Leste, though some effort is required to reach it. Access is off the main road about 45 minutes south of Maubisse, look out for the brown tourism site sign. Allow at least an hour to walk to and from the waterfall along a steep 1.3km path. The path is generally decent, with some steps, but closer to the falls care needs to be taken as it can be slippery. An enterprising local has built a bamboo bridge to access the waterfall, for which payment is required to cross ($1.50 for Timorese and $2 for malae / foreigners).

reviews.name: S Kai
reviews.text:
アイナロの中心から車で30分程。茶色の看板が道路脇に建っています。看板付近に車を停めるスペースがあり、そこから徒歩で片道1時間程です。道は未舗装部分が多いですが、部分的に階段やコンクリート舗装された箇所もあり歩きやすいです。
道中、道を整備していると名乗る男性から通行料を要求されることがあります。最初2ドルと言われましたが、1ドルでも通してくれました（帰る際にはいなくなってました）。
滝の直前、竹の橋が設置されています。滝付近に住んでいる（自称、土地の所有者）おじいさんが設置したもので、通行料は1人1.5ドルです。橋の無い川沿いの道を進むこともできますが、おじいさんに怒られますので竹の橋を渡ることをオススメします。
雨季明けだったため滝壺には入れませんでしたが、凄まじい水量の滝は圧巻でした。
reviews.textTranslated:
It's about a 30-minute drive from the center of Ainaro. There's a brown sign on the side of the road. There's a parking space near the sign, and it's about an hour's walk from there. While much of the road is unpaved, there are some stairs and concrete sections, making it easy to walk.
Along the way, you might encounter a man claiming to be maintaining the road who will ask for a toll. He initially asked for $2, but was happy to let me through for just $1 (he was gone when I left).
Just before the waterfall, there's a bamboo bridge. It was installed by an old man who lives near the waterfall (and claims to be the landowner), and the toll is $1.50 per person. You can also walk along the river without the bridge, but the old man will scold you, so I recommend crossing the bamboo bridge.
Because it was the end of the rainy season, we couldn't enter the basin, but the sheer volume of water was impressive.

reviews.name: Michael Stone
reviews.text: An incredible experience. A steep one hour hike. Hiking shoes recommended. The final section down to the waterfall is muddy and very slippery (and dangerous) when wet. The magnitude and power of the waterfall is amazing. I recommend visiting on a weekday.

reviews.name: John Dooley
reviews.text:
Beautiful waterfall and a lovely walk to get to it.
The place is not well-signposted but going off the map location it is hard to go wrong. The walk up takes less than 30 minutes, but some parts of the trail are pretty gravelly and slippery. Other parts have concrete steps and more were being laid when I was there, so hopefully soon it will be easier to walk on. Take water, there are no kiosks up there or at least there were not at this time.
If you do not have your own transport, you can hire an angguna "mesak" (independently) from Maubisse or Same. I got one by asking around at the market in Same.

reviews.text: Beautiful white sand beach but make sure to check the tide schedule. I arrived early in the morning, thinking I would beat the heat if I hiked/caught a ride after sunrise, but then realised it was low tide as I arrived, which was still beautiful but that meant no swimming in turquoise waters... It seems like it's better to check it out in the afternoon. The road is not the best in some parts and very steep in others, but motorbikes seem ok, car is definitely better. The locals on bikes are usually kind enough to offer you a ride, otherwise the taxi/truck runs between Beloi and Biqueli at busy times like market days or when ferries arrive/depart (I paid $1.5 sharing with others from Biqueli back to Beloi). Otherwise the boat price from Beloi is still set at $70. With a car it's $60.

This is about as beautiful a beach as you will ever visit. The sand is golden, colour of the water is perfect. You can get a little boat here from elsewhere on the island, but it is also less than three hours walk to or from Beloi, for example. Note there are a couple of very steep places on the road, even though the other 95% of the trip is flat, which are hard even on a scooter. The walk between this beach and Beloi is through some beautiful fishing villages.
We did not snorkel here but were told it is ok, though nothing special compared with the many other amazing spots on the island .
