reviews.name: Maria Z
reviews.text:
In the golden light of afternoon, the beach becomes a lively canvas of community life—people playing soccer, strolling along the shore, families gathering and laughing together. It's heartwarming to witness how movement and connection have become such a natural, healthy rhythm in Dili's daily life.

Though swimming isn’t possible here, simply sitting with a cup of coffee, watching the sea, and feeling the warmth of the people around you is a beautiful experience in itself.

A place where the soul of the city reveals itself—not through grand sights, but in the joy of simple moments shared.

reviews.name: Jonty Crane
reviews.text: Had a wonderful three night stay here, easily done as weekend trip away from Dili with Aero Dili (flights Friday afternoon and Monday morning). This is one of the best places I've stayed in Timor-Leste outside of Dili. For $45 you get a large room, with good bathroom, outdoor seating, and a substantial and tasty breakfast. The restaurant food is also great, particularly the curries. It is a little bit out of town, but they will kindly pick you up and drop you off at the airport free of charge. Across the road is a lovely beach, and the mountain scenery behind is quite stunning. Only thing to note is that there are plenty of mosquitos outside so bring protection. Otherwise this is the perfect place to stay in Pante Macassar, highly recommended.

reviews.text: Named after a rock that was spray painted with the name "Bob" at the entrance to a small rocky road through the trees leading to a nice shaded rocky beach.  Great for weekend picnics and wonderful snorkeling and diving too.  There is a wall on the western end of the site with lots of soft and hard coral and if you are lucky you will run into seahorses and spine-cheek anemonefish.  The sandy area just in front of the beach is home to a colony of garden eels and if you are really quiet you can get up close to them before they retreat into their holes in the sand.

reviews.textTranslated:
I had an avocado juice for breakfast. It was listed on the menu for $1, which I thought was a great deal. The combination of the thick avocado and chocolate was delicious.

The espresso I ordered afterward (also $1) was delicious too. The strong caffeine hit me right up.

However, when I went to pay, I was charged $3. I pointed to the menu and pointed it out, but they insisted the avocado juice was now $2. There was no prior explanation, and the cashier showed absolutely no remorse. I think many people have had a similar experience, so please be careful. I didn't get the feeling that the cashier respected the customers at all.

The interior of the shop was very nice with lots of trees, and the drinks were delicious, but the bill ruined everything. If the shop had admitted their fault and apologized, it wouldn't have been such a big problem. It's not about the money, it's about sincerity. I hope they revise the menu as soon as possible.

This huge tree in Tutuala is, without a doubt, the most magnificent natural apiary I have encountered in Timor-Leste. It is absolutely blanketed in full, active honeybee colonies, a truly impressive natural wonder.

Unlike many beehive trees in the region that show signs of local harvesting, this one appears completely wild and untouched, resulting in a phenomenal density of hives.

The local bees here are highly active. Visitors should maintain a respectful and quiet distance to observe these industrious insects and protect the colonies.

reviews.name: Natalia Ciobanu
reviews.text:
A Hidden Historical Gem in Timor-Leste

Maubara Fort is a fascinating piece of Timor-Leste’s history. Perched on a hill, it offers stunning views of the surrounding landscape and the sea. The fort itself, though small, is well-preserved and gives a real sense of the colonial past. Walking around, you can imagine the strategic importance it once had. It’s a peaceful spot, perfect for history lovers and photographers alike. A must-visit for anyone exploring the western part of Timor-Leste!

reviews.name: Alex Gundry
reviews.text:
The old Duth fortifications stand silent under a grand canopy of old trees. The shade was welcome after a morning in the car, in late Spring heat.
Our guide took us up to the the remaining building, which is now a small cafe and a souvenir shop of handmade crafts.
The cafe offered a tamarind drink, which was wonderfully sour, offset with lemonade. Perfect!
There are a few old canons still in place, inviting a wealth of stories from our guide.
Opposite this site are more craft shops, with an impressive selection of local fabrics (Tais).

reviews.name: Md Anjum Islam
reviews.text:
I have visited Atauro Island twice, first in 2025 and again in 2026, and every visit has reminded me why this island is considered one of the hidden jewels of the Coral Triangle.
Atauro is home to some of the richest marine biodiversity in the world, with crystal-clear waters, vibrant coral reefs, and incredible opportunities for snorkeling and diving. Beyond its natural beauty, the island’s communities are deeply connected to marine conservation.
It is encouraging to see Atauro recognized as one of the Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) within the Coral Triangle Marine Protected Area System (CTMPAS). It is also inspiring that the island is progressing toward the IUCN Green List, reflecting its commitment to effective and sustainable protected area management.
If you love nature, marine life, and authentic island experiences, Atauro Island is a destination that deserves a place on your travel list. I hope its unique ecosystems continue to be protected for future generations.

Atauro Island, nestled in the crystal-clear waters of the Timor Sea, is a hidden gem for those seeking an untouched paradise. With its pristine beaches, vibrant coral reefs, and lush landscapes, the island offers a serene escape from the hustle and bustle of modern life.

The island's diverse marine life makes it a haven for snorkelers and divers, providing a mesmerizing underwater world to explore. The coral gardens teem with colorful fish, creating a kaleidoscope of marine beauty. The warm, inviting waters make it an ideal destination for water enthusiasts.

Away from the coastline, Atauro's interior is a tapestry of rolling hills and dense forests, perfect for hikers and nature lovers. The island's rich cultural heritage is evident in the traditional villages, where locals warmly welcome visitors, offering a glimpse into their daily lives and customs.

While the island embraces its natural charm, amenities are basic, catering to those seeking an authentic, off-the-beaten-path experience. Accommodations range from simple homestays to eco-friendly resorts, enhancing the overall eco-tourism appeal.

Atauro Island captivates with its untouched beauty and tranquil atmosphere, making it a haven for those in search of a paradisiacal retreat and a genuine connection with nature and local culture.

Ataúro significa cabra, e é uma ilha quase em estado selvagem, com uma grande diversidade de peixe e corais em abundância e em perfeito estado de conservação. Local de excelência para mergulho autónomo. Rodeada por águas com uma cor azul turquesa, com uma visibilidade excelente onde é possível observar corais duros e moles muito coloridos e vivos. Um mergulho inesquecivel
reviews.textTranslated: Ataúro Island is a hidden treasure in East Timor. Ataúro means goat, and it's an almost untouched island, with a great diversity of fish and abundant, perfectly preserved corals. An excellent location for scuba diving. Surrounded by turquoise blue waters with excellent visibility, it's possible to observe very colorful and vibrant hard and soft corals. An unforgettable dive!

ハトリアの中心部から4WD車（もしくはバイク）などで約45分、そこから徒歩で15分程のところにある全長102mある木製の吊り橋。地元の人によると昔はバイクに乗ったままでも渡ることが出来たそうですが、現在は老朽化のため徒歩のみ渡れるそうです。
中心付近は非常に揺れます。片側に寄ると傾いて怖いので、真ん中を歩くことをオススメします。
木製の床はところどころ隙間があり段差もついています。下は川があるのでスマホなどを落とさない用に気をつけてください。
reviews.textTranslated:
This 102-meter-long wooden suspension bridge is located about 45 minutes by 4WD vehicle (or motorbike) from the center of Hatria, followed by a 15-minute walk. According to locals, it used to be possible to cross it on a motorbike, but now, due to its age and deterioration, it's only accessible on foot.

The bridge sways considerably near the center. It's recommended to walk in the middle, as it tilts precariously on one side.

The wooden floor has gaps and uneven sections in places. Be careful not to drop your phone or other items into the river below.

I predict that in the coming years, this spectacular location will be a must see spot for international visitors to Timor Leste! At just over 3000m elevation you will experience a stunning sunset, sunrise or anytime. This is a magnificent vantage point to see the country from every angle! 360 panorama views the include Betano beach in the south! Our group trekked here from Dili and spent the night at the camp where an outdoor church is located about 30 minutes walk from the mountain top.
You will not regret the effort it takes to get here. It can be cold, so bring some warm clothing.

Banyak bersyukur dunia yang kita nikmati, jauh di periode sebelumnya diperjuangkan dengan darah-air mata dan pengharapan. Jadi, wajib menyambangi "Memorial aos Massacrados de Aileu 1942."
reviews.textTranslated: We visited this historic monument in June 2022. We were traveling from Dili towards Maubisse. We stopped by the monument to see and learn more about it. We also browsed the internet for information about the monument, which was a historical monument from the Portuguese-Japanese war. We are grateful for the world we enjoy, fought for so long in the past with blood, tears, and hope. Therefore, a visit to the "Memorial aos Massacrados de Aileu 1942" is a must.

reviews.name: Jonty Crane
reviews.text: On 31 August 1942 Aileu was invaded by Colunas Negras, the Timorese allies of the Japanese invaders. Five Portuguese soldiers, and a number of civil servants and missionaries, were killed. A sizeable memorial on the main road through town commemorates the massacre. Opposite the monument is an attractive building from Portuguese times, and a pair of statues representing mane (men) and feto (women) in local traditional clothing.

reviews.name: Ludwig Simek
reviews.text:
Anfahrt mit Roller möglich, aber schon eine Herausforderung. Gerade nach Regen ist die Piste sehr schlammig. Teils so tiefe Pfützen, dass man nur Barfuß durchkommt oder eben mit dem Roller. Am Parkplatz campierten an einem Sonntag geschätzt 2.000 Menschen, meist Teenies. Ich bin um 9 Uhr losgelaufen und war um 10:20 Uhr am Gipfel. Weg sehr einfach zu gehen, teils mit Treppen. Auf dem Weg etliche Stände mit Getränken und Suppen. Beim Wandern leben die Teenies ihre Jugendkultur voll aus, hören laute Musik, schreien herum, werfen ihren Müll in die Natur. Ich hab mehrere Tüten davon aufgesammelt, aber da liegt leider noch genug herum. Gottes Schöpfung wird hier völlig missachtet. Ganz anderes Bild am Gipfel. An der Marienstatue wird gebeten und dem Herren gelobt. Alle sind leise und ehrfürchtig. Es ist ein Wallfahrtsort.
Es war schön zu sehen, dass so viele junge Leute Bergsteigen gehen. Die meisten sehr freundlich. Als einziger Europäischer bin ich auf viel Begeisterung gestoßen. Ist sicherlich nicht jedermanns Sache, aber ich vermute, dass es unter der Woche ruhiger ist.
Insgesamt lohnend, aber das mit dem vielen Müll und Lärm ist sehr traurig. Überlegt euch bitte wie sich Jesus oder Maria hier verhalten hätten. Ich bin mir sicher, dass sie diesen Müll und Abfall am Berg nicht gut gefunden hätten.
Und bitte zieht euch feste Schuhe für den Berg an. Keine Schlappen und Sandalen.
reviews.textTranslated:
Getting there by scooter is possible, but quite a challenge. Especially after rain, the track is very muddy. In some places, the puddles are so deep that you can only get through barefoot or by scooter. On a Sunday, an estimated 2,000 people, mostly teenagers, were camping in the parking lot. I started hiking at 9:00 a.m. and reached the summit at 10:20 a.m. The trail is very easy to walk, partly with steps. There are several stalls selling drinks and soup along the way. While hiking, the teenagers fully embrace their youth culture, listening to loud music, shouting, and throwing their trash into nature. I picked up several bags of it, but unfortunately, there's still plenty lying around. God's creation is completely disregarded here. A completely different scene unfolds at the summit. At the statue of Mary, people pray and praise the Lord. Everyone is quiet and reverent. It's a place of pilgrimage.

It was wonderful to see so many young people going mountaineering. Most of them were very friendly. As the only European, I encountered a great deal of enthusiasm. It's certainly not for everyone, but I suspect it's quieter during the week.

Overall worthwhile, but the amount of trash and noise is very sad. Please consider how Jesus or Mary would have reacted here. I'm sure they wouldn't have approved of all this garbage and waste on the mountain.

And please wear sturdy shoes for the mountain. No flip-flops or sandals.

reviews.name: Arthit Yodyunyong
reviews.text:
For an independent traveler get a minitruck (3$)from Taibesi station in Dili. Look for the name „Hatu Builico“ on the trucks. From my understanding there’s a truck at a specific date and time that goes directly to Hatu Builico, the village near the summit. If it doesn’t (that happened to me) tell the driver you‘ll go to Mt. Ramelau. He‘ll drop you at the place called „Fleixa“ about 8 km after Maubisse. There‘s a sign „Mt. Ramelau“ pointing to a very bad unpaved road on the right. If you walk on this road, it‘s 18 km to Hatu Builico. The road is very scenic. In my case I met a villager from Hatu Builico and I just walked with him. He used cow paths and walked in straight line from Fleixa to Hatu Builico. This reduces the distance and took me only 2 hours to reach Hatu Builico but I wouldn’t attempt this if I was alone.
In Hatu Builico the villagers are very nice and friendly. Some can speak English and can help you find a hotel. From the village it‘s straightforward 4 km to the trail entrance and another 4 km to the summit.
If 18 km walking back to Fleixa doesn’t appeal to you, your hotel can arrange a transport either motorbike or 4WD for you. I paid 30$ for a ride with a motorbike to Maubisse.

May 2026, 2 Malaysians come in 2 bikes.
Tutuala beach only has guest houses operating, Valu is one of it, Praia is closed. We paid usd26 for the beach fronting hut, usd5 each for dinner with rice, eggs, veggie, fish and banana. Usd2 each for breakfast of popmie baso noodle, eggs, coffee and tea. 1.5L water is usd1.
The beach is isolated from tutuala village, no entertainment, shops and restaurant. The area only has the guest house operators and fisherman or boatman who can bring you to Jaco island on usd10 per pax.
When weather is bad, waves are high, no transfer to Jaco island.
The beach is beautiful, clear blue water.
At around 9pm, we saw locals catching small fishes at the beach after the tide subside, it was an interesting experience.
the road from fuiloro to tutuala of 39km is very rough, unpaved, paved with big potholes, it took us 1.5hours on average 30kph. Please be mentally prepared.
There was no data coverage in the area with Telemor.
The guesthouse owners are helpful, we communicate with them using bahasa Indonesia.

reviews.name: Nicole Marenghi
reviews.text:
This is definitely my favourite guest house in Timor Leste. It’s a cooperative which means that it is run from the community and the money goes back into that.
The ladies couldn’t speak English but they were super welcoming! One night is 25$ dollar for a double room. dinner is 5$ each and breakfast is 2$ each.
We had an amazing time and wish we stayed longer. You can get a fishing boat to Jaco for 10$ return.
Getting back to Lospalos is the hard bit. We were lucky cause a family that was staying in the guesthouse was going back to Dili and they gave us a ride. Otherwise you probably need to hitchhike or walk the 8 km until Tutuala, spend the night there and try to get a truck back to Lospalos the day after.

Anyway I really recommend staying at the Valu Sere Cooperative and support their beautiful community.

reviews.name: Caleb Betts
reviews.text: Stayed for three nights (6/8/24-9/8/24). The man who runs the place, Tiu João, was very kind and helpful. Showed us how to get to the beach where the boats were going to Jacó and when it was time to leave was able to get someone to take us up to Tutuala for $10 each. The place was very clean, food was solid, and consistent access to electricity (only thing lacking is good internet which is an infrastructure problem). Of course, coming to Valu in general requires either really good planning or really good luck if you aren't using private transportation, but it's unquestionably worth it. Jaco is a special place with the whale bones we found right as we got off the boat, the shells the size of our heads on the beach, the unique double horned deer that inhabit the island, and the breathtaking coral reefs straight out of a national geographic documentary. If you get the chance, come! $30 a night and reasonable meal prices, we paid $150 for three nights including three breakfasts, three dinners, one lunch (all for two people), and a couple snacks.

reviews.name: Jan Wojtkowski
reviews.text:
I paid 35$ for 1 person for a night with dinner - coffee with baked banana 3$ in the morning.

It’s a lot for Asia but for such a remote plac I say it’s fair price.

reviews.name: Silvio Alves
reviews.text: Bele sai fatin refreshing

reviews.name: Gigi
reviews.text: If you’re coming to Valu beach stay at Valu Sere! The two women who were running it while we were there are so lovely and welcoming they ushered us in to our cosy and simple hut with food quickly to follow despite us arriving unannounced quite late in the evening. Food costs are on top of the price of the room with fish cooked fresh from whatever was caught that day. Reasonably priced for what you get and the pristine and untapped location.

reviews.name: Victor Lin
reviews.text:
Good place to stay with basic $5 vegetarian lunch and dinners that does not vary at all during your stay. No meat option, although apparently if you manage to get fish from somewhere they can cook it for you - and there are definitely loads of fish just off the beach in the crystal clear waters and coral reefs.

I paid $30 a night for a room with a fan and a shared toilet block. I needed to bring my own toilet paper and there is absolutely no cell phone reception anywhere in the area and no WiFi. You have to go halfway up the mountain towards Tutuala to get reception.

There also aren't any ATMs nearby that take foreign bank cards, so bring enough cash for your intended length of stay.

reviews.name: Kerry Riddell
reviews.text:
A great place to stay and it's helping with the generation of the community's income. The road from Tutuala to Jaco is now paved so access is very easy.
The rooms were clean and the food was great. We were offered a hut for $25/night but opted for the bigger room at $30/night. Breakfast $2, lunch and dinner both $5 and good portions. Staff very friendly and welcoming. Easy to arrange a boat to Jaco by turning right at the T-junction instead of left to the accommodation.

reviews.name: Soumitro Roy
reviews.text: Eco friendly guesthouse. The houses here have thatched roofs and floors. Walls are wooden. There are two guesthouses next to each other on this beach. You need to see the sign post carefully to reach out to the right one, that you are looking for. This one is named as Valu Sere. Managed by the community. Facilities are basic. There is only one common toilet shared with all guests of the day. They provide a mattress on the floor, bed sheets, mosquito net and a rack to keep your stuff. Electricity available. All the rooms are slightly elevated. Always ask for a fan. Otherwise they will forget. Night until 1 am it's hot inside the rooms, even if you don't close the window or door. They need to arrange for another window in the rooms for cross ventilation. You can experience amazing sunrise from the beach just outside your room, provided there is no obstructions to your sight by the clouds. Located about 225 kms from Dili, a very pleasant place to stay for one night after you return from Jaco island.

reviews.name: leonard fong
reviews.text: Basic huts a long the beach but has the worst over priced food.

reviews.name: Jean Charieras
reviews.text:
4 jours à rien faire c'est bon. Surtout dans une communauté de femmes locales généreuses qui s'occupe bien de vous. C'est rustique, propre avec moustiquaire et ventilateur.
A comparer le ressort d'à côté vous rempli votre bouteille pour 1 dollars 50!
reviews.textTranslated:
Four days of doing absolutely nothing is perfect. Especially in a community of generous local women who take such good care of you. It's rustic, clean, with mosquito nets and a fan.

Compare that to the resort next door where you can fill your water bottle for $1.50!

reviews.name: Josep M Gracia
reviews.text:
Un lloc fantastic.
Comoditats, zero, pero la sensació de tranquilitat i aillament, el tracte dels cuidadors del lloc, que a mes es una coopetarita dels habitants de Tutuala es genial.
I per si fos poc, tens Jaco Island al devant, on pots arribar amb una barca de pescadors i disfrutar d'una illa verga, amb un fons marí fantastic practicament sol
reviews.textTranslated:
A fantastic place.
Amenities, zero, but the feeling of tranquility and isolation, the treatment of the caretakers of the place, who are also a cooperator of the inhabitants of Tutuala is great.
And as if that were not enough, you have Jaco Island in front of you, where you can arrive with a fishing boat and enjoy a verga island, with a fantastic seabed practically alone

reviews.textTranslated: A very beautiful place, worthy of a postcard, the meal however not great.

reviews.name: Mikke Palvanen
reviews.text: Great place for relaxing a few days.  The staff didn't really speak any English so maybe bring a tetun dictionary with you,  absolutely no service with Telemor here. Prices and info listed in Mark Henderson's review are correct as of Feb2019.  I traveled here in one day from Baguia (18h)  back to Dili in one (15h) and wouldn't really recommend it for anyone.  Maybe okay if you're already around the area or have your own car but hitchhiking/going with public bus is just too rough and you'll need to stay for at least three nights.  Then again hitchhiking there and back is possible but just super slow and rough. Also walked the 8km from and to Tutuala, back in rain, and never have I sweated so much. On the other accommodation they offered to drive to Tutuala for 10$ and Lospalos 20$, if you negotiate with some locals beforehand you can maybe organize also something,  but even they seemed to be asking crazy prices...  The cave was large but nothing spectacular if you've already seen caves,  maybe spend the 10$ on some beers by the beach instead :) all in all I had a great and surreal experience being there all by myself. The food they offered seemed to get better by every meal and the amount of it was always massive

reviews.name: Diogo Branco
reviews.text: Local muito simples e rudimentar mas muito acolhedor. Cabanas com separadores que fazem um número variado de quartos, mobilado com uma cama de casal, uma rede mosquiteira e uma pequena cómoda. Casa de banho partilhada numa cabana à parte, com banho de púcaro. Sem nenhuma preocupação excessiva com a limpeza! Se encomendado com algumas horas de antecedência, preparam refeições baratas e saborosas. Pequeno almoço timorense. Preço de 20 usd por quarto.
reviews.textTranslated: A very simple and rudimentary but very welcoming place. Cabins with partitions that create a variety of rooms, furnished with a double bed, a mosquito net and a small chest of drawers. Shared bathroom in a separate cabin, with a bucket shower. No excessive concern for cleanliness! If ordered a few hours in advance, they prepare cheap and tasty meals. Timorese breakfast. Price of 20 USD per room.

reviews.name: Sukesan Moorthy
reviews.text: They didn't understand english so well, it was difficult to communicate. We felt that we disturbed them when we ordered food. We were both sick all night after dinner ( big bean soup with little bones). The place is good and the bed is simple.

reviews.name: Mark Henderson
reviews.text: Great for adventure seekers who want to get away from it all.  As of January 2018 prices were $20/room (stand-alone hut), $10/tent, $5/dinner, $5/lunch, $2/breakfast, $10/person for a cave tour.  The beach is pristine, glassy blue and calm.  The huts are bamboo with a thatch roof.  There is a Western and Asian style toilet, which doubles at a bucket-shower area.  You can buy bottled water and beer (I suggest bringing some of your own water just in case).  The food was standard for rural Timor.  Nothing special.  However, you can buy a fish from the local fishermen, and for a small fee they will cook it for you.  You can build a campfire on the beach.  At low tide, there are lots of rocks.  It isn't a great swimming/snorkeling beach.  For that, either hike south near the fishing boats or go to Jaco Island itself.  We had the place to ourselves for 2 nights, but then on the third a bunch of youth on motorbikes showed up and rudely played their music very loud late into the night then again in the morning.  The co-op (village) runs the place.  They rotate workers each week, so you never know who you will get.  All in all, its remoteness, natural beauty, fascinating caves, and exquisite marine environment makes it well worth the effort.  Just come prepared  as if you were camping just in case.  No credit cards are accepted here.

reviews.name: Joel Cooper
reviews.text: The rooms ($20/night) feel like camping in a big tent, but the beautiful beach access makes this establishment worth it. A few traditional bungalow huts with porches are taken first, and there are three connected rooms with even less privacy for overflow. Rooms have dirty sheets, a mosquito net, an outlet, a light, no fan, and a door that does not lock. There are three shared bathrooms with plenty of complimentary water for traditional showers. We came on a holiday weekend, so all rooms were taken and loud music played all night. Many people were camping. The meals are very good ($5/person + price of fish), and the staff are very friendly. The picturesque white sand beach is right there. Rent a mask and snorkel from the hotel ($5/day) and swim 10 meters out to the beautiful reef. Rent a life jacket from the hotel ($10/day) and walk 10 minutes south along the beach to the fishing boat captains who will take you over to Jaco ($10 r/t) during daylight hours.

Beto Tasi beach is the best place to enjoy a sunset, walk in the beach and to swim. The water is amazing. Clear, warm and not much waves. In the afternoons, the people starts by to show up. It’s interesting to see all those kids playing by their own in the beach amd taking dips or to see the local fish men community working. A very pleasant place for a enjoy the view and the time.

reviews.name: Adhityo Wicaksono
reviews.text: I went here for a quiet dinner time with my friends, although we went here a bit late (around 7 pm) and the guy who works on the grill was already home. But it’s okay. My friends ordered Bitoque - beef steak served with sunny side up egg, white wine gravy, fries and salad, and I ordered Arroz Tomate com Bife (tomato rice with beef in tomato based sauce). For the drink, we ordered fresh orange juice and mineral water. The meals arrived late (around 45 minutes after we ordered), but at least we still have our drinks and I wandered around to hear some waves at night and the view of starry night. The sauce on Bitoque was amazing. I love my meal (Arroz Tomate com Bife) as I love the tomato rice, the beef was also good. I think this place is a hit for lunchtime or daytime in general, as at night, it’s quiet on my visit. There are some of the owner’s dogs wandering around as well. The restaurant view was okay.

reviews.name: KB
reviews.text:
Located on the way to Liquica town, this resort is ideal for a rustic weekend getaway at its dark sandy beach. Good for family (plenty of pool, hammock). The restaurant offers nice meals with a beautiful sea view and facility (clean toilet + a shower room), though the kitchen and drink service can be slow, so it's best to order in advance.

The restaurant allows overnight camping for about USD 10 per tent (on high ground  beside the beach, so you don't have to worry about high tide), so bring your own gear if you're up for a night under the stars. The restaurant also serves breakfast for guests of the nearby Alma Do Mar Resort.

Overnight parking is available at the resort, making it convenient for campers. Just be prepared for a bumpy ride on the last stretch of unpaved road from the main highway—manageable even without an SUV.

reviews.name: Jonty Crane
reviews.text:
One of Timor Leste’s two islands (with Atauro Island), Jaco is an uninhabited, 10km2 island about 700m off the eastern end of mainland Timor-Leste, home to beautifully clear waters off a white sand beach. There isn’t really anything on the island, other than an impressive set of whale bones to the south of where the boats land, and a thick bush interior with no paths, but it is a quiet and relaxing place. Just off shore are several patches of coral, though less diverse or life filled than those around Atauro Island, and with stronger currents. It isn’t possible to hire snorkel gear locally so bring it with you. There are a surprising number of deer, given that there is no reliable fresh water supply on the island. It is an important site for birds, including rare birds such as the great cuckoo dove and the orpheus fathead. Jaco Island is considered sacred by Timorese and staying overnight is not allowed, but it is a popular place to visit for a few hours.

Jaco Island is reached by small boat from the southern end of Valu Beach (where there is accommodation), which costs $10 per person for a return trip. Pay on your return. The channel between Valu Beach and Jaco Island may look swimmable, but the currents are very strong. The crossing can be rough and life jackets may be advisable (though not available locally). It is best to visit in the morning when the sea tends to be calmer. Let the boat operators know how long you want to be on the island (a couple of hours is usual), and they’ll come pick you up, though timings may be approximate.

Crocodiles are regularly spotted by Valu Beach so it is advisable to stay out of the water. The strong currents deter, but not entirely, crocodiles from visiting Jaco Island. There have been no publicised fatalities but near misses have happened, so enter the water at your own risk.

Getting to Jaco Island requires some effort, and while technically doable in 2 days, it is much better to spend 3 days and stay in Baucau or Com on the way there or back. It 6-8 hours drive from Dili with your own transport, which every tour operator in Timor-Leste can organise. The roads are fine to Com, then vary between fine and terrible. Allow 2-3 days if taking public transport as buses from Dili to Lospalos arrive after the erratic (mostly) daily bus from Lospalos to Tutuala leaves. From Tutuala it is a steep 8km walk down to Valu Beach.

Other transport options offered by the Cooperativa Pescas O Sol Nascendo Tutuala (+670 7760 9031 or +670 7718 2335) include a boat trip around Jaco Island for $20 per person, and a return journey by boat from Com for $100 per person. Note that everything boat related is weather dependent.

reviews.text: During our stay in East Timor we chose to stay at Tibar Beach Retreat for a few nights to enjoy the tranquility of getting out of the city and take in the views during our drive from the city to Tibar Beach.| The accommodation was very nicely presented, traditional, air conditioned and comfortable. reviews.name: karengr56
reviews.text: Our stay at Tibar Beach Retreat was a highlight of our recent stay in East Timor.|Our host Alice was amazing; very friendly and and not only drove us in and out of Dili at no cost but she was an excellent 'tour guide' with perfectly spoken English.|Alice went over and above expectations of good customer service.|The retreat itself is set in a very peaceful spot with beautiful tranquil gardens. The accommodation was very comfortable, well presented and traditional with lovely views of the bay from the verandahs and the dining area. The restaurant on site served good food and the staff were very pleasant. |We thank Alice sincerely for her daily assistance and friendliness and highly recommend staying at this accommodation.

reviews.name: Absydabsy
reviews.text: The hospitality shown was warm and inviting, we felt more like personal guests than paying customers. The owner went out of his way to take care of us - from airport pick ups/drop offs, taking us into town whenever we wanted, organising tours and even opening the restaurant earlier to suit our needs. Whilst we had booked for 3 nights, we checked in really early and checked out late. Ordinarily at other hotels you would be charged at least an extra fee, but they wouldn't hear of it here as much as we insisted! Room was beautiful and comfortable, and they even accommodated our toddler. The restaurant was equally as good - I can recommend the "Chocolate Surprise" if you've got a sweet tooth. The only downsides to this place is the location and lack of Wifi (but that's across the country). It is a little out of town. That might be ok for most, but it was harder for us with a child. But overall, I would happily stay there again.

Maybe the nicest place to stay just outside of Dili. Nice clean rooms with air conditioners, TV, a view, a fan, stylish furniture, and a hot kettle. The rooms come with a deck overlooking the ocean. It's a great spot for a romantic sunset.

The restaurant frequently runs out of some of their dishes. So when you order, have option B and C as a backup.

reviews.text: I've stayed here a few times now and every time has been fantastic. If you only have one night in Dili this is the best value place you can find. They pick you up from the airport and are happy to drop you off again and once you are there it is a little bit of luxury in Timor. The views are great and the sheets have that lovely crispness to them. Over the years it has clearly been well loved (it could probably do with a new mattress and mosquito net in the room) but it's still great. There is a new road out the front so traffic has increased but it still drops off at night so we didn't find it too much of a bother. We would both happily stay here again.

reviews.text: This is my second,visit to tibar beach. I like It for several reasons. First is that it is peaceful. The food in the restaurant is great and I had the best long island tea I have had in ages. Finally the owners, Alice and rui, are two of the loveliest people you will ever meet in south East Asia, or anywhere for that matter.  They will pick you up from the airport and take you into town  on request for free. I am back I dili in a month or so and I will be staying here again

reviews.name: hidehikok
reviews.text: The third time I stayed at Tibar. I have very much enjoyed my hobby of Amatuer Radio everytime. Every radio operator is always waiting for our CQ DX from Timor Leste. I have had thousands of calls from all over the world. I could make morse key communications with Asia , North/South America, Western/Eastern Europe, Central/South Africa, Australia and even with Antarctica ! in a day and night. Amazing !  The hosts Rui and Alice are always nice to us and all people in the resort are very friendly. I love this place.

They accept us to build up some big antennas necessary to enjoy global radio communication. And yes! here is generally one of the best place in Timor. The beautiful view, cute restaurant, nice walk on the hills...etc. Even Dili residents come here in weekend to rest.  I love here.

reviews.text:
ALOLA ESPERANSA PROVIDE A MARKET FOR LOCAL WEAVERS GROUPS AND PROVIDE NEW HOPE FOR THEM TO PRODUCE HIGH QUALITY PRODUCTS.

In 2005, Alola Foundation established Alola Esperansa project with goal to support the program of Alola Foundation especially the Economic Development program to assist Timorense weavers develop small industry and improve the status of women by purchasing their textiles. The industry’s aim is to provide an outlet for weavers to sell their traditional textiles “tais” and also provide employment especially for women.

Alola Esperansa has two sections, retail and production.  On retail section, Alola Esperansa operates one outlet in Dili at the Alola Foundation building. This outlet provide different kind of quality hand woven Tais Textiles from across Timor-Leste, Virgin Coconut oil, Pottery, Baskets,, Baby Bag, Tote Bag, Cushion Cover, Tais jewelry pouch, Passport Folder, wallet, book marks, Scarf, clothing, water bottle holder, candle & lamp shade, woven basket, pencil case, postcard, kaibauk, jewelry, traditional house,  Timorese coffee, etc. On this outlet, customers can order special design for tais products.

title: Maddog Adventures - Explore Timor Leste
ownerDescription: Maddog Adventures is a privately owned and operated business that supports the economic development of rural communities in Timor-Leste through adventure tourism. We are outdoor adventure specialists skilled in Canyonning, Treking, Cultural Tours, Mountain Biking and educational travel for schools and universities. Our goal is to provide premium adventure tourism experiences that have a positive impact on Timor-Leste’s people, culture and natural environment and in the process bring you closer to nature and leave the places we visit better than we found them. Do you love adventure and travelling off the beaten track? Do you enjoy the journey as much as the destination? Timor-Leste is the go to country for intrepid travellers.

reviews.name: Jonathan Kennedy
reviews.text:
An incredibly unique experience with Mad Dog Adventures on the La Rende trip. The trip was much more than just a hike, the level of engagement with the local communities made it feel genuinely immersive and meaningful.

From sharing local food and meeting people along the way, to the incredible vistas and challenging but rewarding track, every part of the experience felt thoughtfully put together. The guides were fantastic extremely knowledgeable, friendly and always willing to help. Everything ran seamlessly in the background, which made it easy to focus on enjoying the experience.

It’s not often you get an adventure that combines history, culture, community and some genuinely spectacular scenery. Highly recommend Mad Dog Adventures to anyone looking for a unique hidden gem of a hike.

reviews.name: Matthew Booth
reviews.text:
Recently completed the La Rende! track through Timor Leste with Maddog Adventures. Easily one of the most amazing hikes I have completed, from the track it self, the people and communities along the way and the staff of Maddog Adventures.

The trek itself went through some absolutely breath-taking countryside. Timor Leste's landscape changes with each valley crossed and every clear patch of trees provided an awesome photo opportunity. Difficulty of the trek was accurate to Maddogs rating of Moderate to Advanced.

The trek includes nightly stops at mostly guest houses - all of which were in very good condition. Meals were always provided by local families of the villages organised through Maddog, which gave us a good taste for some of the local cuisine of Timor Leste. The people and communities we moved through were extremely nice and friendly, always ready pull a chair out when a rest was needed or offer up their porch for shade along the track.

Finally the staff of Maddog were outstanding. All, from drivers to guides, were extremely professional and competent in their job.  Everything was always set up to schedule and ran very smoothly. It is obvious they have conducted a lot of work to make this trek as enjoyable and well planned as possible.

Highly recommend for a once in a lifetime experience!

reviews.name: Tarryn O'Hehir
reviews.text: What an amazing trip! Thanks to Sam for organising and to Ollie for being our awesome guide. We had the best time and can't wait to come back again

reviews.name: Daryl Browne
reviews.text:
I booked a 6 day tour through a travel agent and was extremely happy with the coordination and delivery of the itinerary put together at very short notice. My guide Ollie was great. Lot's of knowledge and experience to lead me on an East Timorese adventure. The trip included spectacular scenery through the mountains to Hato Bulico and climb to the summit of Mt Ramelau for a perfect sunrise experience. An overnight taste of Atauro Island included a wonderful stay at Barry's Place overlooking the water and another perfect beach sunrise. Snorkeling off Beloi was wonderful, with plenty of colour.
The accommodation in Dili was high level and a perfect location. I can highly recommend Maddog Adventures for touring in Timor-Leste.

reviews.text:
Explore we did! We experienced beautiful mountains, waterfalls small rural villages, beaches, markets, museums, local produce,5* hotels, guest houses, historical sites and still just skimmed the surface of this amazing country and culture.
Maddog Adventures were fantastic guides- knowledgable and engaged. Thank you HIGHLY RECOMMENDED

reviews.name: Kathy Cash
reviews.text: It was the best experience I have had in a very long time. It was packed with excitement, adrenalin, great tour guides, beautiful scenery, village shopping, authentic Timorese food, great company and beautiful Timorese people. Climbing Mt Ramelau was my highlight. Maddog Adventures who took the group on this tour were always organised and were very professional in their delivery. Recommend them highly.

reviews.name: Lydia Kooman
reviews.text: Amazing day tour with Liesel, Ollie, Gida and the team! Fantastic local knowledge, plenty of water, sunscreen, and laughs provided on board. The team was friendly and attentive throughout. Could not recommend this tour more highly!

reviews.name: Morganne Ashley
reviews.text: My husband and I really enjoyed our 2D/1N Mt Ramelau tour with Maddog Adventures. We had a great time and I can't recommend this tour highly enough! Booking the tour was very easy, our guides were fantastic, the food was good, and the room was comfortable. If we have the chance to return to Timor Leste, we will definitely book another tour with Maddog Adventures.

reviews.name: Scott Ricketts
reviews.text: On my way home from East Timor and had to share my experience with Maddog Adventures on the Le-Rende hike I just completed. This is a land and people that are full of life and heart and the landscapes we hiked through were nothing short of mind blowing. I had no idea that Timor Leste had such diverse environments and was blown away to he hiking through Eucalyptus and Casuarinas shortly after in tropical jungle with huge bamboo, lush ferns and coffee plantations. Highly recommend Maddog Adventures for the way the whole trip was run and the level of care and organization by the whole team. A truly eye opening experience through a land of surprises.

reviews.name: Jesse S
reviews.text:
I participated in a multi-day trail run lead by Maddog Adventures + Tour de Trails in August 2024 and cannot recommend the experience highly enough.

Timor-Leste is a diamond. The natural beauty and diversity of the geography is outrageous. At least once daily I would be stopped in my tracks by a jaw dropping vista as we made our way along the La Rende! Trail.

The Maddog team is top notch. We were well supported in personnel, supplies and tips on how to safely traverse. The guides (Ollie, Elizabeth, Marcel, Dom) are all Timorese and so generous with stories about the progress and opportunties they see for Timor-Leste.

The run itself was challenging, but well planned. The most challenging days were followed by lighter days, either in distance or terrain and there were multiple guides with the group to allow for people to move at the right pace for them each day.

If you are looking to explore a new place, challenge yourself physically and don't mind roughing it, look no further. Maddog Adventures will treat you to a life highlight.

reviews.text: És un bon lloc per venir a passar el dia a la plateau. Servei excel·lent, varietat de carta per menjar, I la platja està neta.
reviews.textTranslated: It's a good place to come and spend the day on the plateau. Excellent service, variety of food on the menu, and the beach is clean.

reviews.name: Raphael B Harel
reviews.text: Spent a really nice couple of nights in Lauhata. The owner Carlos and his team are super friendly and helpful. They made every effort for any question we had. Location is a short drive away from Dili, really a perfect escape from the hustle and bustle. Rooms great value for money.

reviews.name: Jose Felix
reviews.text:
A 30 minutos de carro ou mota, da cidade de Díli, tem à disposição uma praia limpa, mas, a maioria das vezes a água é turva. O espaço de restauração e bar apresentado, é  limpo, mas, nem sempre com um serviço célere.
Para almoço foi opção peixe escalado e grelhado, muito bom, mas, a preço acima do razoável, tendo em conta a mão de obra barata, e o pescado à porta.
Os quartos, e não esquecendo  local, tem um preço elevado para a fraca decoração num conforto equivalente a um hotel mediano.
O espaço proporciona um ambiente tranquilo para casais e famílias, mas, não vai além do mencionado.
reviews.textTranslated:
Located a 30-minute drive or motorbike ride from the city of Dili, there is a clean beach available, but the water is often murky. The restaurant and bar area is clean, but the service isn't always quick.
For lunch, we opted for grilled and scaled fish, which was very good, but the price was above reasonable, considering the cheap labor and the fact that the fish was caught right outside.
The rooms, and not forgetting the location, are overpriced for the poor decor and comfort equivalent to a mid-range hotel.
The space provides a tranquil environment for couples and families, but it doesn't offer much beyond that.

reviews.name: Delivio Soares (Kivo)
reviews.text: My family and I went to Lauhata Beach Scape to witness the solar eclipse on April 20, 2023. The place was packed with people, and there was live music and cocktails to enjoy. The food and drinks were great, and the service was excellent.

reviews.name: Andrew Warner
reviews.text: A chill place to spend the day. Restaurant, bar, coffee, loungers, beach, shade!? What more do you need! Escape the hustle and bustle of Dili with a quick ride to paradise!

reviews.name: Nai2
reviews.text: Nice green open space here perfect for a weekend away or a lazy Saturday afternoon. Silence is golden and this place is great to get away from noisy Dili, although a little more expensive.

reviews.name: Jonty Crane
reviews.text: Stopped for a delicious and quickly served lunch at this beautiful waterfront hotel and restaurant. The food, service, and atmosphere was better than the nearby Uma Knua. Highly recommend if you are passing through, or want to escape the hustle and bustle of Dili

reviews.name: Teófilo António Soares Maia
reviews.responseFromOwnerText: Thank you Teo.

reviews.name: johnsI8949LK
reviews.text: Quiet out of the way place.|Close to Dili, we decided to stay here just for a night to check it out.|Only 6 rooms available in huge grounds.|Room was fine, clean, basic, nothing missing, water was warm, not hot. No bar fridge.|We had room #1 close to the beach. Very dark room, good for sleeping.|Lounges on the cement for relaxing and some table chairs and benches on the beach.|Beach is black sand but kept very clean by the hotel staff first thin in the morning.|No pool, but we swam in the sea, bit difficult to get out as little dumping waves, slight undertow current.|Whales and dolphins have been spotted here.|Very good sunsets  and the  beach is safe  for long walks.|We had dinner which was ok, but as per normal in East Timor the menu is too westernised for our liking.|Breakfast was fine and the coffee very good.|I believe the hotel gets busy of weekends and public holidays with day trippers.

reviews.name: PhtevenChinoLover
reviews.text: Lauhata was amazing, out of all the resorts in Timor-Leste this is by far the best! The resort was unreal, everything from the rooms to the food and location was just perfect. Rooms were comfy and clean with good aircon, the grounds were amazing and well kept, the beach in front was stunning with crystal clear water and good snorkeling. The staff and service were second to none, the food was incredible, and to top it all off they made amazing coffee. If you are looking for somewhere to go and relax and unwind, this place is hard to beat. Avoid the hustle and bustle of Dili, head straight to Lauhata. Also the highlight of the trip was Bendu, the main man! He went above and beyond to make sure we had an amazing stay and trio, was such a legend, organised everything else we needed and was such a wealth of knowledge for any questions we had. Can’t thank him enough!

reviews.name: Kimberley Low
reviews.text: Lauhata is a perfect place to unwind and simply do nothing - bring a book, play some beach volleyball and watch the beautiful sunset. My partner and I stayed for a night and had a lovely time. The staff are very hospitable and the food was quite excellent. Thank you Carlos and team for the lovely experience.

reviews.name: JSS
reviews.text: I stayed there recently and really enjoyed my time. It truly was a nice escape and not far from Dili. The drive there was pleasant and I like that they provided transport. One less thing for me to figure out. The cost is very reasonable. The room had everything I needed for the night. The grounds were serene and well-kept, and I felt safe and secure there. I enjoyed walking along the coastline and exploring the grounds. The food was great and they offered many options.

reviews.name: judybdarwin
reviews.text: The rooms are clean and air conditioned with en suites, the bed was comfortable with a sitting area on each verandah to relax on. |Carlos and Bendu make you very welcome. Breakfast was included in the rate.|Meals can be purchased anytime you want and were great and a good price.|Recommend the gin and tonic with dragon fruit!|Will definitely be returning. |

reviews.name: Tim Tin
reviews.text: Arrived at 11:30, partial food (rice salad) arrive at 1 pm (1 hour 30 min), the main course Satay and Rendang another 30 min…staff brings only two plates each trip, waitress never heard of serving platter capable of holding multiple plates.  Very poor and slow service for very expensive price…stick with Bali restaurants where staff understand customer service

reviews.text: Great place for weekend escape. Lauhata has own transport offered to the visitor, at a cost of 20 usd per person. Beach is not good for children, but is compensated by the large space available for leisure.

My husband and I paid $100 for a package of an overnight stay at their hotel with excellent dinner choice (delicious tomato cream soup, grilled pork and fish, cheese cakes, 1 bottle of wine) and also a decent free breakfast. All was worth it 🥰 Thank you Lauhata.

reviews.name: Dee to the Eee
reviews.text:
Lovely spot with good food and service. Had breakfast today with coffee and juice and all were enjoyable. Trainee servers were very polite and attentive. Toilets have had an upgrade since I was last here. A wonderful spot for a lazy brunch on the beach or in the portico areas.

Edit 2 - Valentine’s Weekend 2021
We took advantage of the Valentines packaged that included decorated room, wine, dinner and breakfast. Rooms are basic but comfortable, clean and have AC and en-suite.

Edit 3 - Midweek getaway 2022
One of my favourite and easiest places to get away from the hustle and bustle of Dili. It is nice and quiet during the week and on the weekends they setup extra tables in the shade on the large grass area.

Overall, Lauhata is a gem of a place to escape to. It’s is about 25km west from Dili. Yes, sometimes food and drink items are not available due to seasonal availability but this is the same country wide. I have now stayed several times and when I have travelled here as a lone, malae female, I have always felt safe. There are only a few grassed areas in Dili and this is the best. Families and large groups often come to spend the day. I book accommodation via WhatsApp or by calling.

reviews.name: Trip.com Member
reviews.text: While there’s no major negative thing about this place, there is also no major positive. It stands out like a much better looking “Hollywood style motel”. The breakfast is adequate. The location is more or less ok. The fact that Dili needs people to have or arrange transportation continually does no favour for the hotel, but has nothing really to do with the hotel itself, of course. It is just that fact that there is nowhere really walking distance from it.

reviews.name: Trip.com Member
reviews.text: Good, stay is just for layover..

reviews.name: Karin Sinniger
reviews.text:
We stayed here on three separate occasions during our time in TL. Every time was a pleasure. And we actively looked forward to returning here.

The staff are absolutely amazing and friendly. They will do their best to help.

The Filipina receptionists are efficient and welcoming. They will gladly keep any luggage you don’t need safely for your return.

Responses to arrange airport pick up are very quick. They were always very prompt.

If you need to leave early, they will bring a packed hot cooked breakfast to your room on time.

We had a problem with air conditioning in our room one night and were told the maintenance staff had gone home (understandably). Lo and behold at 9:30 PM they actually came to fix the problem so that we could sleep well in Dili’s  heat. Truly remarkable.

Breakfast is a cooked breakfast with beautifully cooked eggs and beans. Plus fruit. Fresh fruit juices are also available for an extra fee.

We were two but had booked the two bedroom ground floor apartment for our stays. WOW! Huge with one double bed and two twins and two bathrooms plus kitchenette. We even had a handy washer and dryer.(You can buy washing powder at the little convenience stores almost across the street from the hotel). Everything was very clean, water was hot, and the WIFI worked well.

There a decent bakery/cafe  a five minute walk from the hotel and lots of coconut and fresh produce vendors nearby.

The hotel was a small pool.

The only suggested improvement would be to have their shuttle available to guests for short hops across town for a fee like some other hotels in Dili offer, given that it takes so long to get a local taxi. (Microlet taxi bus services are easily available from close to the hotel if need be.)

reviews.name: NAOKI NISHIMORI
reviews.text:
この日のレートでディリの中でトップ5くらいには高いホテルだった。

スタッフの接客は良い。

ただWi-Fiが繋がらない（対応してくれたので良いけど）
シャワーのお湯が出ない（対応されず）
など不満点も。

立地はビーチには近いものの付近に飲食店がほぼないので注意。
これは事前に調べてわかっていたので良いけど。
ルームサービスも終わるのが早いので
何か食べ物を持ち込んだ方が良い。

価格の割にはあまり良くなかった。
現地スタッフの愛想の良さでカバーされている感じがするので、
運営側が設備をしっかり保全して欲しいと思う！
reviews.textTranslated:
This hotel was among the top 5 most expensive in Dili at the rates that day.

The staff service was good.

However, there were some drawbacks, such as the Wi-Fi not working (though they did fix it), and the shower not having hot water (which wasn't addressed).

The location is close to the beach, but there are almost no restaurants nearby, so be aware of that.

I knew this beforehand, so it was fine.

Room service also ends early, so it's best to bring your own food.

It wasn't very good for the price.

It felt like the friendliness of the local staff was making up for it, so I hope the management will properly maintain the facilities!

reviews.text: Convenient location to walk to the beach or Avenue de Portugal to catch a microlet. Comfortable accomodation, good breakfast, and amazing air conditioning when you need it. Staff were super helpful, and the airport transfer was convenient.

reviews.text:
Was in Timor Leste for nearly three weeks. Spent the first night and the last three nights here. Glad I did!
Very nice room. Spacious, clean and knock you over air-conditioning and ceiling fans. I had a kitchenette. Staff could not have been any friendly, cheerful and accommodating. The breakfast ladies tried to teach me Tetum as best they could. This American is lazy with language and I was coddled. No issues at all. Nearby bakery & cafe. Otherwise it was the included breakfast with a large selection or nice dinner ordered in. VALUE for my money!!!
Handy to the beach. The upper floors have a view. I did not use the spotless pool. When I return to this town. The Palm Beach Hotel will be my choice for comfortable, safe and enjoyable lodging. Highly Recommend. Even the fellows at the gate were great to be around.

reviews.name: Gerdo Trada
reviews.text:
Highly Recommend Arbiru Beach Resort!

I’ve stayed at quite a few hotels around Timor-Leste, and while many of them look new and modern, I still prefer Arbiru Beach Resort when it comes to overall value and service.

Check-in was quick and smooth. I originally asked to pay by card, but they kindly explained that credit cards aren’t commonly used in Timor-Leste, and only one bank accepts them with high fees. The hotel doesn’t work with that bank, so they only accept cash. Just a heads up make sure to bring enough cash with you!

My stay was great overall. The staff were super friendly and helpful, the food was delicious, the pool was lovely, the Wi-Fi was fast, and my room was spacious and comfortable. The breakfast team was especially attentive, always checking in to see if I needed anything.

The resort itself isn’t brand new and could use a bit of work on the outside, but the rooms were spotless, nicely painted, and cleaned daily. Laundry service was also included in the room rate, which was a nice bonus.

They also offered free airport pickup and drop-off, which saved me $30 total (since taxis here cost about $15 each way). Prices in Timor are higher than in Bali, but after a few days, I understood why almost everything has to be imported.

Honestly, I feel like this hotel has so much potential. If tourism in Timor picks up, I think Arbiru could be truly amazing. For now, it’s already a fantastic place to stay, especially if you’re looking for comfort, great service, and a relaxing vibe.

reviewContext.Rooms:
Simple but Cozy:
The decor was simple, nothing too fancy, but it felt really cozy and relaxing. Perfect for chilling out after exploring Dili.

One of my favorite parts daily laundry service was included in the rate. So convenient, especially for longer stays.

It was also nice and quiet at night, so I slept really well. No noise from the hallway or outside, which was a big plus.

reviews.name: Julie Jules
reviews.text:
No. Just no!
Waiting for check-in took forever, almost an hour and no card payment, even though the online app showed it as an option. 😑

The staff was super slow and didn’t understand what I was saying. I booked through an online app, but they tried to charge me the offline price. Even though I eventually got the app price, it was still annoying.

The location was far from the city center, and there was literally nothing around except the hotel and industrial buildings.

No lock. On my first day, I wanted to go out, but the door wouldn’t lock. Luckily, there was an extra lock from the inside. Since I canceled the rest of my stay except for that one night, I just left it. When I checked out, I informed the staff that the door couldn’t be locked from the outside. They said it was automatic.
Well, yeah, normally hotel doors lock automatically, but the problem was that this one didn’t. Then they kept making excuses, saying it had to be locked from the inside. Like… I’m leaving the room, so how the hell am I supposed to lock it from the inside???

Requested a hairdryer but no hairdryer. No amenities at all. The water was boiling hot and couldn’t be adjusted to cold. 😑

I came back from dinner around 10 PM, and the garden lights were off, almost pitch black.

I’ve been to less developed countries before, but I have never seen a hotel like this, let alone one that dares to call itself a resort.

When I visited in April 2024 the original building, a colonial era villa, was undergoing restoration work paid for by the Japanese. Work should be completed by the end of 2024.

The menu at the restaurant is somewhat different compared to other Chinese restaurant in town. The owner shall consider to set up more stand fans. The weather in Dili is too hot, for table in which without ceiling fan and stand fan. We ended up soaking wet after having lunch.

They have tasty Chinese food here like what I had in Beijing. Chef & owner is from mainland China.

Beware, portions are humongous. Mapo tofu + rice was more than I can handle for myself.

Recommend to come in a group and have shared dishes.

reviews.name: Charles Tan
reviews.text:
The place is located on the road just after the traffic light. Place to park is usually road side opposite the shopfront. The ambience of the place is quite nice with shade from trees there. They have private rooms if you are looking for a private dinner.
Food wise the cooking is not bad. Some recommended dishes are the claypot brinjal, the fried or steamed fish, fried tomato eggs etc. The price are not to expensive so a good place to go for some authentic chinese cooking. Alcohol is served here..

reviews.name: RL
reviews.text:
Cosy cafe within the Pateo compound with free covered parking for the first hour. The smell of authentic curry draws you in even from metres away outside. Staff are friendly and English-conversant.

We had:

Mango lassi - refreshing!
Chicken momos - juicy and delicious.. I would come back just for these!
Plain and butter naan - perfectly acceptable
Chicken biryani - big portion and satisfying meal!
Aloo matar and butter chicken - well balanced flavour and nicely sized portions

We will be back!

reviews.name: Jose Felix
reviews.text:
Para amantes de cozinha nepalesa, o restaurante "Evereste" é simples, de economia familiar, mas simpático. Boa confecção nos pratos disponíveis e com qualidade.
Preços acessíveis.
Colaboradores simpáticos com dificuldade no Tétum e português, mas, com um inglês, perceptível.
Aceita encomendas e pode levar para casa.
reviews.textTranslated:
For lovers of Nepalese cuisine, the "Evereste" restaurant is simple, family-run, but friendly. Good quality dishes are prepared.

Affordable prices.
Friendly staff who have difficulty with Tetum and Portuguese, but speak understandable English.
They accept orders and offer takeout.

reviewContext.Parking: Perto do restaurante, pago para além de um tempo limite. Nem sempre é fácil arranjar lugar
reviewContext.Wheelchair accessibility: Localizado no piso térreo. Com estacionamento controlado e disponível.

reviews.name: S Kai
reviews.text:
東ティモールで唯一のネパール料理屋さん。
店内は10席程の小ぢんまりとした空間です。
ランチでモモ（ネパールの餃子）を食べました。蒸してあって皮モチモチ。具材は肉汁たっぷりで野菜の甘みの中にパクチーがほのかに感じられ、スパイスの効いたアチャールソースとの相性抜群。
食後にデザート（グラブ・ジャムンとラスグッラ）頼もうとしたらどっちも無いとのことで残念でした。
駐車場と駐車場は敷地内にあります。
reviews.textTranslated:
This is the only Nepalese restaurant in East Timor.

The restaurant is small and cozy, with only about 10 seats.

For lunch, I had momo (Nepalese dumplings). They were steamed, giving them a chewy texture. The filling was juicy, with a hint of cilantro amidst the sweetness of the vegetables, and it paired perfectly with the spicy achar sauce.

I tried to order dessert (gulab jamun and rasgulla) after the meal, but unfortunately, neither was available.

There is parking available on the premises.

reviewContext.Parking: 駐輪場は敷地内にあります。

reviews.name: Sa Da
reviews.text:
No one told me I could grab a steaming plate of authentic Nepali Momos (Kathmandu more than Tibetan/Darjeeling style) in Dili.

The tomato achar is exactly like back in Nepal. No idea how they recreated that perfectly.

Thukpa is tangy and satisfying but for noodle soup aficionados - let me honest, broth is ok but noodles less so. So g ahead and grab a bowl like I did. Just expect more out of the Momos!

title: Timor Plaza
ownerDescription: Timor Plaza is more than a retail centre; it is a lifestyle centre where everything for the home and family is available in an attractive, inviting and convenient shopping environment, with easy access and parking. The Timor Plaza Centre Court has also become a renowned arena for social, cultural and commercial activity. It is now the intention of Dili Development Lda. to create five more buildings to accommodate a balanced range of retail, accommodation, office and tourism facilities, constituting a vibrant commercial community that will drive private sector development in the capital for years to come.

reviews.name: Debbie K
reviews.text:
I have to say, Timor Plaza Hotel was such a pleasant surprise! I honestly wasn’t expecting it to be as nice as it was and was really impressed. The rooms are spacious, the beds are super comfortable and the staff are incredibly friendly and welcoming.

The Sky Bar was definitely a highlight. We had dinner there — BBQ meats, salad and fries — and the food was amazing. There was a live band playing, a great atmosphere and the place was packed. The outdoor area, with all the lights and trees, was beautiful, and the views over Dili were absolutely amazing.

We had such a great stay here and I would highly recommend Timor Plaza Hotel if you’re staying in Dili!

Der Food Court ist gut, aber viel zu teuer.
Sonst ist ebenfalls alles sehr teuer. Teuerer als in Deutschland und überhaupt kein Vergleich zu Indonesien.
reviews.textTranslated:
We got our SIM cards without any problems and strolled around. Unfortunately, it's far too noisy for a pleasant shopping experience. Loud music is playing on every corner.

reviews.text:
동티모르에 방문했을 때 시원하게 커피도 마시고 쇼핑도 할 수 있었던 장소입니다.
버스 터미널. 호텔 등 여러 기능이 복합적으로 갖추어진 장소입니다.
인도네시아 쿠팡에서 버스로 도착했을 때 저녁 6시쯤 이곳에 왔구요.
일요일에는 오전에 예배드리고, 점심 후에 이곳 티모르 플라자에 와서 맛있게 커피 마셨네요.
아참 동티모르는 미국 달러를 사용합니다.
모든 일정을 마치고 인도네시아 쿠팡으로 복귀하는 버스도 이곳 티모르 플라자 뒷편에서 탔습니다.
시간은 오전 6시 30분입니다.
여튼 티모르에서는 쇼핑. 커피타임. 버스 등 여러 가지를 이곳에서 경험했네요.
깨끗하고 좋습니다.
아침에 조깅하면서도 이곳을 지나갔는데 가끔 러너들이 이 근처를 뜁니다. 조금만 걸어가면 바닷가도 나오거든요.
굿.굿.
추천합니다.
황
reviews.textTranslated:
This is a place where I could enjoy a refreshing cup of coffee and go shopping when I visited East Timor.

It is a complex facility equipped with various functions, including a bus terminal and a hotel.

I arrived here around 6 PM after coming by bus from Kupang, Indonesia.

On Sunday, I attended church in the morning, and after lunch, I came to Timor Plaza here to enjoy a delicious cup of coffee.

Oh, by the way, East Timor uses the US dollar.

After finishing my entire itinerary, I also took the bus back to Kupang, Indonesia, from behind Timor Plaza.

The time was 6:30 AM.

Anyway, in Timor, I experienced various things here, such as shopping, coffee breaks, and taking the bus.

It is clean and nice.

I passed by here while jogging in the morning, and sometimes runners run in this area. The beach is just a short walk away.

Good. Good.

I recommend it.

Hwang

reviews.text:
Hot and delicious Singapore Malaysian style dishes!

We especially like the sweet and sour pork, sweet and sour fish with rice, crispy noodles and seaweed soup. The homemade ice lemon tea is legit as well.

They also have a lunchtime buffet option (rice + various dishes) for a very reasonable price.

The owner and his wife are humble, friendly and hospitable.

Overall a great place to have meals and it also accommodates large size groups easily.

Found one of my comfort food, sweet & sour pork, cooked to perfection, tender meat, crunchy on the outside and sweet sour sauce was great !
It was quite a good portion for the price.

Uncle Tan said they serve breakfast such as fried bee hoon, yu tiao, curry puff and such. For lunch, buffet style meal.

This has to be one of the best options to get Singapore / Malaysia chinese food in Dili.
